## Detailed findings

### Critical

#### DFA-001 — Omitted/wildcard projection and search bypass read-field authorization

**Evidence: static.** TypeScript only checks fields when `select` is an explicit array (`datafn/server/src/validation/authz.ts:145-192`), while projection returns every schema field when selection is omitted or wildcarded (`datafn/server/src/execution/query/select.ts:122-148`). The search route executes without the normal query authz validator (`datafn/server/src/routes/search.ts:264-305`); cross-resource search returns raw rows when select is absent and fetches on namespace rather than row/field policy (`datafn/server/src/execution/search/cross-resource.ts:43-53,127-177`; `datafn/server/src/execution/search/native-fallback.ts:59-70,126-220`). Python repeats the explicit-select-only check (`datafn/python/datafn/authz.py:210-275`), fetches full rows and projects only if select/omit exists (`datafn/python/datafn/handlers/query.py:119-124,161-183,226-230`), and clone/pull return visible raw rows (`datafn/python/datafn/handlers/sync.py:108-141,242-282`).

**Impact:** restricted fields and, on search paths, private records can be disclosed. Omitted select is canonically “all base fields” (`datafn/docs/content/docs/dfql/select.mdx:12`; B01 `REQUIREMENTS.md:113-142`), so this is not an obscure malformed input.

**Required fix:** derive the projection from policy even when selection is omitted; recursively expand and authorize wildcard/relation selection; run the same resource/row/filter/field authorization for search; project clone/pull payloads; add negative tests for omitted select, `*`, nested wildcard, restricted filters, private search rows, and Python parity.

#### DFA-002 — Relation writes bypass field authorization because auth reads the wrong payload member

**Evidence: static.** The public wire/runtime model accepts `relations?: Record<...>` (`datafn/server/src/execution/mutation/dfql.ts:38`) and the executor iterates `mutation.relations` (`datafn/server/src/execution/mutation/relations.ts:121-166`). The authorization helper instead reads obsolete singular `mutation.relation` and allows the operation when it is absent (`datafn/server/src/validation/authz.ts:419-458`).

**Impact:** ordinary valid relation mutations bypass `permissions.write.fields` and can modify links that drive inherited sharing. This affects direct mutations, transactions that reuse the validator, and any sync path that expects parity.

**Required fix:** authorize every key/item in `relations`; delete the obsolete shape; use one validator for direct/push/transact; test viewer/editor/owner, restricted relation fields, inheritance consent, multiple relation keys, and malformed values.

#### DFA-003 — Clone, pull, and reconcile permit request-body actor spoofing

**Evidence: static.** Each route spreads the request payload and overwrites `actorId` only when the trusted extractor returns a value: clone (`datafn/server/src/routes/sync.ts:81-96`), pull (`datafn/server/src/routes/sync.ts:192-207`), reconcile (`datafn/server/src/routes/sync.ts:545-559`). If no provider is configured or extraction returns undefined, a body-supplied actor survives. Push is safer because actor is passed separately (`datafn/server/src/routes/sync.ts:431-445`).

**Impact:** a caller can impersonate a creator/grantee for selective/private data, and audit attribution can be forged.

**Required fix:** strip all identity fields from decoded bodies before dispatch; pass a trusted actor out-of-band; fail closed when private/shareable sync requires an actor; add no-provider, undefined-provider, spoofed-body, and cross-namespace tests.

#### DFA-004 — WKWebView bridge lacks an origin/frame/navigation trust boundary

**Evidence: static.** `DatafnWKWebViewBridgeHost` attaches a generic script message handler and dispatches matching messages without checking `frameInfo`, origin, main frame, content world, navigation, or a session capability (`datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnWebViewBridgeHost/DatafnWKWebViewBridgeHost.swift:79-110`). The dispatcher validates protocol/method shape and exposes privileged remote/sync methods (`datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnWebViewBridgeHost/DatafnBridgeDispatcher.swift:384-410,680-703`), but handshake merely compares metadata and establishes no authenticated state (`datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnWebViewBridgeHost/DatafnBridgeDispatcher.swift:727-801`). The runtime can attach native-authenticated remote handlers (`datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnAppleRuntime/DatafnAppleRuntime.swift:425-454`).

**Impact:** any compromised document, injected script, or subframe able to post to the handler can access native storage and native-held credentials. Actual exploitability depends on host navigation policy, which is external and unverified.

**Required fix:** allowlist scheme/host/origin, require main frame and an isolated content world where possible, bind a random per-navigation capability after handshake, invalidate it on navigation/background/config changes, and add adversarial subframe/cross-origin/stale-session tests. B31 `SEC-001` is a **spec gap** because it requires method/protocol validation but not caller provenance.

#### DFA-005 — Swift native sync sends the wrong push envelope and may acknowledge rejected work

**Evidence: static.** Swift posts a raw mutation array (`datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnServerSync/DatafnServerSyncEngine.swift:267-280`), and its test asserts that array (`datafn/swift/Tests/DatafnServerSyncTests/DatafnServerSyncEngineTests.swift:126-133`). The TypeScript endpoint requires an object with `clientId` and `mutations` (`datafn/server/src/routes/sync.ts:291-315`). B31 `SYN-002` requires Swift to own canonical seed/clone/pull/push/reconcile.

**Impact:** native DataFn-server sync cannot push to the current server contract. A permissive/mock success envelope can cause Swift to acknowledge local changelog work that the server did not apply.

**Required fix:** send the canonical envelope, validate the canonical per-mutation response, acknowledge only successful/deduped mutation IDs, retain failures, and test against the real TypeScript route rather than a shape-only mock.

#### DFA-006 — Swift clone ignores server pagination, then deletes valid local state and marks ready

**Evidence: static.** The server automatically pages oversized clones and can return before loading joins (`datafn/server/src/execution/sync/clone.ts:210-305`). Swift models `next` but not the server’s `paginated` signal (`datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnServerSync/DatafnServerSyncEngine.swift:25-31`), makes one clone request (`datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnServerSync/DatafnServerSyncEngine.swift:435-461`), deletes local records missing from that response (`datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnServerSync/DatafnServerSyncEngine.swift:470-481`), treats absent joins as empty/deleted (`datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnServerSync/DatafnServerSyncEngine.swift:495-520`), then writes cursors/hydration-ready state (`datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnServerSync/DatafnServerSyncEngine.swift:483-548`).

**Impact:** datasets beyond the server page limit can lose valid local records and joins and advertise a complete replica that is incomplete.

**Required fix:** page until complete, stage the snapshot, preserve omitted resource/join sections, atomically swap only after every page validates, and leave hydration non-ready on interruption. Add >10k record/join, crash-between-pages, duplicate-page, and resume tests.

### High

#### DFA-007 — iCloud native mode cannot satisfy canonical batch/hydrating queries

The client routes batch queries and hydrating/not-started resources through `remote.query` (`datafn/client/src/query.ts:136-165,221-255`). iCloud mode deliberately installs unsupported remote handlers (`datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnAppleRuntime/DatafnAppleRuntime.swift:443-454`), while B31 `QRY-001` explicitly requires iCloud batch queries to be satisfied by the native runtime (`REQUIREMENTS.md:114-124`). **Static FAIL.** Implement a native local query handler with the remote adapter contract or change routing without changing public semantics.

#### DFA-008 — Canonical `$or` is advertised but rejected by the TypeScript server

The intent defines `$or` (`datafn/.conduct/intent/dfql.intent.md:233-245`) and docs advertise it (`datafn/docs/content/docs/dfql/filters.mdx:181-223`). The server validator rejects it (`datafn/server/src/validation/query.ts:714-737`) and a test enshrines rejection (`datafn/server/src/validation/__tests__/validation.test.ts:922-950`). Local/Python behavior therefore differs from remote TypeScript. **Static FAIL of B01** `QUERY-002`**.** Implement the advertised AST or remove it through an explicit breaking spec/docs/type migration.

#### DFA-009 — Public mutation types/docs advertise bulk forms the server rejects

`DFQLMutation` exposes `id: string | string[]` and `records[]` (`datafn/core/src/dfql.ts:29-52`); docs and intent show these shapes (`datafn/docs/content/docs/dfql/mutations.mdx:10-32`; `datafn/.conduct/intent/dfql.intent.md:478-499`; `datafn/.conduct/intent/mutation-sample.json:20,69,86`). Server validation requires singular IDs/records for operations (`datafn/server/src/validation/mutation.ts:318-345`). **Static FAIL.** Either implement each advertised bulk form with bounds/atomicity/results or narrow the public contract and publish a migration.

#### DFA-010 — Idempotency is cross-tenant and non-atomic

The server creates one store using literal namespace `datafn` (`datafn/server/src/server.ts:522-525`). Database keys contain that constant plus `clientId/mutationId`, not the resolved request namespace (`datafn/server/src/execution/idempotency-db.ts:18-40,76-109`); memory keys omit namespace too (`datafn/server/src/execution/idempotency.ts:66-106`). The interface is separate `get` then `set` (`datafn/server/src/execution/idempotency.ts:18-31`), so concurrent identical requests can both execute. **Static HIGH.** Include resolved namespace in a unique key and use an atomic claim/lease/result state inside the mutation transaction.

#### DFA-011 — Atomic transactions silently degrade to partial sequential writes

`atomic` defaults true (`datafn/server/src/execution/transact.ts:41-54`). The implementation uses a transaction if available, but catches “not supported/not implemented” and falls through (`datafn/server/src/execution/transact.ts:105-171`) to sequential execution that preserves earlier writes on failure (`datafn/server/src/execution/transact.ts:174-227`). Idempotency writes can also occur outside the database transaction callback (`datafn/server/src/execution/transact.ts:80-89`). **Static FAIL of B01** `TX-001` **and B04** `TX-ATOMIC-001`**.** Reject unsupported atomic requests and only publish idempotency after commit.

#### DFA-012 — Direct mutation and push have divergent authorization and side effects

Push maintains an independent operation switch. Delete records a row/change but omits the direct path’s permission cleanup (`datafn/server/src/execution/sync/push.ts:347-352` vs. `datafn/server/src/execution/mutation/execute.ts:328-357`). Push share/unshare/relate paths (`push.ts:540-660`) do not reproduce direct relation-inheritance/consent behavior (`execute.ts:620-731`). Direct mutations can persist before inheritance/change tracking later fails (`execute.ts:668-731,766-821`). **Static HIGH.** Use one transactional mutation core and an outbox/change record, with direct/push/transact parity vectors.

#### DFA-013 — Retention configuration can prune current data and ignores tenant namespace

Config reaches startup/periodic pruning without integer/non-negative validation and uses literal `datafn` (`datafn/server/src/server.ts:280-299,338-350,432-453`). A negative day count produces a future cutoff (`datafn/server/src/execution/sync/change-tracking.ts:539-548`; `datafn/server/src/execution/idempotency-db.ts:64-73`). B14 `RET-003` requires rejection of negative/non-integer values (`datafn/.conduct/specs/2026-02-24-audit-fix-k9r4m7x3-spec/REQUIREMENTS.md:271-281`). Tests cover omission, not malicious values (`datafn/server/__tests__/retention.test.ts:193-211`). **Static FAIL.**

#### DFA-014 — IndexedDB namespace encoding collides and migration paths can hide/delete data

Namespace sanitization replaces only colons with underscores, making values such as `org:user` and `org_user` collide (`datafn/client/src/adapters/indexedDbStorage.ts:110-145`). Upgrade preserves v1 stores but switches reads to per-resource v2 stores without migrating data (`datafn/client/src/adapters/indexedDbStorage.ts:300-307,389-430`). When dynamic version exceeds a cap, it deletes the DB and resolves `onblocked` as success (`datafn/client/src/adapters/indexedDbStorage.ts:350-365`). **Static FAIL of B08** `IDB-001`**.** Use injective encoding, an atomic copy/checkpoint migration, and never report blocked deletion as success.

#### DFA-015 — JavaScript clone marks partial pages ready and ignores server auto-pagination

Applying any clone page marks hydration ready (`datafn/client/src/sync/apply.ts:62-90`). The engine only loops pages when client-configured `pageSize < 1000`; default clone performs one request and ignores `result.paginated/next` (`datafn/client/src/sync/engine.ts:577-620,705-766`). It then forces omitted tables ready (`datafn/client/src/sync/engine.ts:622-630`). **Static HIGH.** Stage/page/finalize atomically and treat server pagination signals as authoritative.

#### DFA-016 — Offline query semantics differ from remote semantics

Offline aggregation applies a fixed group-key order and ignores requested sort/limit/offset/cursor, returning null next cursor (`datafn/client/src/offline/aggregate.ts:116-131`). Normal offline queries omit count/omit/full cursor semantics and return null next cursor (`datafn/client/src/offline/query.ts:90-110`). **Static HIGH.** One typed query changes result as hydration changes. Move canonical query semantics into shared core or explicitly reject unsupported local features.

#### DFA-017 — `switchContext` can close the replacement client’s reused storage

Without a storage override, context switch carries forward the current adapter, creates a replacement, then destroys the previous client (`datafn/client/src/client.ts:1837-1875`). Adapter destruction can close a resource the replacement now owns. **Static HIGH.** Use a storage factory per namespace or explicit reference-counted ownership; test switches with reused IndexedDB/memory/custom adapters.

#### DFA-018 — Python package parity remains incomplete despite a green suite

**Verified:** 308 Python tests passed. **Static gaps:** config only admits schema/db/authorize/plugins/logger/limits and routes only query/mutation/transact/seed/clone/pull/push (`datafn/python/datafn/server.py:11-23,48-103`); many-many relations derive obsolete `fromKey/toKey/foreignKey` forms instead of canonical `joinColumns/fkField` (`datafn/python/datafn/relations.py:41-85,115-179`); field auth only examines explicit selection (`authz.py:210-275`); mutation can acknowledge after change tracking errors are logged/swallowed (`datafn/python/datafn/handlers/mutation.py:433-447`); query loads the full resource before filtering (`handlers/query.py:161-168`). Package metadata targets Python >=3.8 but this run exercised only 3.9 and CI currently only 3.11 (`datafn/python/pyproject.toml:5-13`). Mark deferred surfaces explicitly and add a cross-language contract suite.

#### DFA-019 — Swift schema/storage drops semantics and health can normalize away mismatch

`DatafnRuntimeSchema.Resource.Field` contains only name/type/required and the resource omits permissions/capabilities/default/nullable/readonly (`datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnCoreDataStore/CoreDataModelBuilder.swift:54-84`). Direct list reads all rows (`datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnCoreDataStore/DatafnCoreDataStore.swift:546-559`), and observation/search rebuild consume those unfiltered lists (`datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnAppleRuntime/DatafnAppleRuntime.swift:385-393,840-859`). Metadata initialization writes the configured schema hash before health compares it (`DatafnCoreDataStore.swift:1189-1219` vs. `876-912`), so mismatch can be normalized away. **Static HIGH.** Define supported schema projection, reject unsupported semantics, and compare/migrate before overwriting metadata.

#### DFA-020 — Explicit scale requirements remain unmet

Aggregate grouping uses an unbounded map (`datafn/server/src/execution/query/aggregate.ts:33-56`) despite B18 `SCA-009`. Backward pagination copies/reverses the result set (`datafn/server/src/execution/query/execute.ts:72,133`) despite `SCA-010`. Offline changelogs append without the required cap in memory and IndexedDB (`datafn/client/src/adapters/memoryStorage.ts:299-317`; `indexedDbStorage.ts:671-700`) despite `SCA-011`. Many-many relate still performs one upsert per item even when batch capability exists (`datafn/server/src/execution/mutation/relations.ts:199-242`) despite `PER-004`. **Static FAIL.**

#### DFA-021 — Release, workspace, CI, and docs QA are not coherent

Root workspaces include client/cli/core/docs/extfn/server/svelte but omit `datafn/swift-bridge` (`package.json:21-27`), despite B31 `PKG-001`; release metadata includes it (`release-packages.json:69`), while the lockfile has no workspace link. CI covers JS, Python, and docs but no Swift (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:65-200`); root scripts contain only FileFn Swift tasks (`package.json:43-58`). The Swift package depends on a local SearchFn path (`datafn/swift/Package.swift:48-50`). B30 `QA-001` mandates `npm --prefix datafn/docs run docs:audit`, but docs scripts expose only dev/prebuild/build/start (`datafn/docs/package.json:5-10`). SPv2 conformance silently skips if prerequisites are missing (`datafn/server/src/__tests__/conformance/spv2-conformance.test.ts:57-64,299-302`). `swift-bridge/package.json:1-34` lacks normal license/repository/bugs/engines metadata. **Static release blocker.**

### Medium

#### DFA-022 — Sharing V2 configuration is module-global

`configureSpv2` stores configuration in module state (`datafn/server/src/execution/migration/spv2.ts:17-25,97-114`), and every server construction mutates it (`datafn/server/src/server.ts:298-299`). Two server instances in one process can change each other’s authorization/migration behavior. Make configuration instance-scoped and pass it through execution context.

#### DFA-023 — WebSocket authentication contract conflicts across spec, docs, and code

`addClient` trusts host-supplied auth context and explicitly requires the caller to reject unauthenticated upgrades (`datafn/server/src/ws.ts:264-274`). B18 `SEC-001` requires `addClient` itself to validate and close 4401 (`REQUIREMENTS.md:164-174`), while newer namespace design/docs delegate host authentication; `datafn/server/README.md:666-679` is stale. Resolve the spec conflict and make one enforced upgrade adapter the documented default.

#### DFA-024 — DataFn does not wrap accepted adapters with its schema

Repository architecture requires functions that accept `@superfunctions/db` adapters to call `wrapWithSchema` internally. DataFn imports/uses only `wrapWithRowLevelNamespace` around the incoming adapter (`datafn/server/src/server.ts:12,311-335`). This leaves schema adaptation dependent on consumer configuration and conflicts with the shared-package contract. Compose schema and namespace wrappers internally; keep any direct adapter-schema option as a compatibility escape hatch.

#### DFA-025 — Determinism depends on locale, wall clock, and random sources

Core sorting uses host `localeCompare` for values and ID tie-breaks (`datafn/core/src/sort.ts:56-67`). Number validation rejects NaN but accepts infinities (`datafn/core/src/validate.ts:79-84`). Server mutation/sync paths call `Date.now` directly (`datafn/server/src/execution/mutation/execute.ts:100-122`; `sync/push.ts:83-105`), and client mutation IDs use time plus `Math.random` (`datafn/client/src/mutate.ts:161`). B04 explicitly required their removal. Inject clock/ID factories throughout and define binary/code-point string ordering.

#### DFA-026 — Database failures can become successful empty results

`DbDataStore` catches load errors and substitutes empty collections (`datafn/server/src/execution/db-store.ts:82-104` and similar branches). Clone count/fetch failures can likewise produce empty pages/cursors (`datafn/server/src/execution/sync/clone.ts:223-288`). This can turn an outage into a destructive “authoritative empty snapshot.” Propagate typed failures and never advance cursor/readiness on incomplete reads.

#### DFA-027 — Relation-path filters are not fully covered by field authorization

Filter authorization checks the root/base field path (`datafn/server/src/validation/authz.ts:338-357`) but does not prove policy enforcement for every target field traversed through relation filters. Even when returned fields are redacted, restricted target values can be inferred by membership/count. Resolve relation paths through schema index and authorize each traversed target field.

#### DFA-028 — Programmatic search API accepts caller-selected namespace

The programmatic server search API accepts `params.namespace` directly (`datafn/server/src/server.ts:987-1016`) rather than resolving through the configured namespace provider. This API may be intended for trusted server code, but it is a security-sensitive footgun and inconsistent with HTTP. Separate a clearly named privileged API or require an instance-bound namespace context.

#### DFA-029 — Code generation can produce colliding identifiers

Type generation converts arbitrary resource/join names to PascalCase without collision detection (`datafn/cli/src/codegen.ts:32-45,88-93,151-158`), so names such as `foo-bar` and `foo_bar` collide/merge. Drizzle variable sanitization replaces all non-identifier characters with underscores, also without collision detection (`datafn/cli/src/drizzle-codegen.ts:43-46,276-285,421-424`), producing duplicate `const` declarations. Reject canonical collisions or allocate deterministic escaped identifiers and add hostile-name compilation tests.

### Low

#### DFA-030 — Each server instance installs process signal listeners

Server construction installs signal listeners (`datafn/server/src/server.ts:981-985`) and cleanup is tied to close paths (`datafn/server/src/server.ts:938-939`). Repeated instances in tests/serverless processes can accumulate listeners and warnings. Make process-hook installation opt-in or centrally reference-counted.

## Spec conflicts / spec gaps

 1. **WebSocket authentication conflict:** B18 requires `addClient` to authenticate through the former auth-context provider; B19/B20 remove that API and current docs delegate upgrade auth to the host. No precedence rule resolves this.
 2. **Namespace migration conflict:** B17 uses `multiTenant`/auth-context terminology; B19 renames it; B20 explicitly removes all legacy bridges. Historical requirements cannot all pass simultaneously at the current surface. B20 should be declared superseding for API presence, with B17 retained only for behavior.
 3. **Python surface ambiguity:** early bundles describe broad TypeScript/Python parity, while later notes defer WebSocket/search/reconcile/REST/GraphQL/namespace-provider integration. The package and docs need a normative supported-surface table.
 4. **Mutation shape conflict:** current core types/intent advertise arrays, while server validation implements singular bodies and some route-level batches. No version/capability negotiation explains the divergence.
 5. **Select/auth gap:** specifications define omitted select as all base fields and explicit-field authorization, but do not clearly require policy-derived projection for omitted/wildcard selection. This omission enabled DFA-001.
 6. **Search auth gap:** search specs focus on candidates/options/determinism, not parity with row/field/filter authorization. The alternate route therefore lacks a normative security matrix.
 7. **Bridge caller-provenance gap:** B31 `SEC-001` covers method/protocol/payload safety but not origin, frame, navigation, or capability binding.
 8. **Multi-instance SPv2 gap:** sharing specs do not prohibit module-global configuration or require isolation between multiple servers in one process.
 9. **Atomic fallback gap resolved by older intent, violated by code:** B01/B04 require externally observable all-or-nothing atomicity, but code treats adapter support as permission to degrade silently.
10. **Shared schema-wrapper gap:** DataFn specs focus on row-level namespace wrapping and never incorporate the repository-wide requirement to wrap accepted adapters with the function schema.
11. **Native schema compatibility gap:** B31 does not state how unsupported permissions/capabilities/default/nullable/readonly fields are rejected or preserved by Swift.
12. **Release evidence gap:** bundles declare package/workspace/docs requirements but no single release gate covers JS, Python, Swift, docs links, examples, package manifests, and registry dry-runs.

## Cross-cutting audits

### Security and authorization

**Conclusion: blocked.** Validation includes important positives—schema indexing, default-deny policy behavior in many TS paths, recursive pollution-key checks, namespace wrapping, empty-namespace rejection, readonly capability stripping, and bounded search input—but critical alternate paths bypass the intended policy. DFA-001-DFA-004, DFA-010, DFA-012, DFA-022, DFA-027, and DFA-028 must be resolved before production.

### Determinism

**Conclusion: not demonstrated.** Stable ID tie-breaks and sorted output exist in many paths, but locale-sensitive comparison, direct clocks/random IDs, partial pagination, global configuration, and inconsistent offline/remote semantics violate equal-input/equal-output guarantees. Real cross-runtime golden vectors were not executed.

### Limits and resource control

**Conclusion: incomplete.** Payload/query/select/filter/search and several batch limits exist. However aggregate groups, offline changelog, backward-copy memory, many-many batching, Python full-table queries, and negative retention configuration remain unsafe. No benchmark or stress test ran.

### Error handling and canonical envelopes

**Conclusion: incomplete/fail-open.** Routes generally use canonical envelopes and redact stacks, but DB/clone errors can become empty success, direct mutation side effects can precede later failure, Swift can acknowledge invalid push results, and Python can swallow change-tracking failures. Operational truth is therefore not guaranteed.

### Compatibility, versioning, and migrations

**Conclusion: blocked.** IndexedDB v1/v2 visibility and namespace encoding are unsafe; global SPv2 state complicates migrations; native metadata can overwrite mismatch before health inspection; types/docs/runtime mutation shapes differ; Python/TS/Swift surfaces and versions are not tied by a conformance gate.

### Operational readiness

**Conclusion: unverified and currently insufficient.** No real SQL adapter, WebSocket upgrade, browser offline transition, WKWebView, CloudKit, native auth refresh, registry, or production-like load was exercised. Health/logging surfaces exist statically, but several failure paths report misleading success.

### Release and packaging

**Conclusion: blocked.** Swift bridge workspace/lock mismatch, no Swift CI, absent docs-audit command, local Swift dependency, incomplete manifest metadata, and silent conformance skips prevent a defensible release claim.

### Swift / Python / TypeScript boundaries

**Conclusion: contract tests are mandatory.** The Swift push/clone bugs and Python relation-shape drift are boundary failures that unit tests with local mocks did not catch. Canonical JSON fixtures should be consumed by TS, Python, and Swift, including negative/auth/pagination/partial-ack vectors.

## Positive invariants observed

These are useful foundations, not a production sign-off:

* **Verified:** Python tests: 308 passed in 0.47s; collection found 308 tests.
* **Static:** server validates schema at construction and centralizes schema indexing.
* **Static:** recursive prototype-pollution keys are rejected in core/server validation paths.
* **Static:** query, payload, select, sort, filter, relation-depth, search, batch, and WebSocket queue/heartbeat limits exist in substantial parts of the TS server.
* **Static:** TypeScript’s normal query path derives namespace through the provider, rejects empty namespace, wraps database access for row-level namespace, and applies private-row visibility logic.
* **Static:** server-owned capability fields are stripped/injected in normal mutation paths.
* **Static:** sequence and idempotency database implementations exist, and many result sorts use an ID tie-break.
* **Static:** relation target existence is batch-validated; many-many uses deterministic composite IDs.
* **Static:** server close clears timers/providers and WebSocket structures.
* **Static:** Swift bridge dispatcher whitelists method names, validates protocol/schema metadata, and restricts envelopes to JSON types.
* **Static:** native search has digest/rebuild/persistence architecture and deterministic resource ordering.
* **Static:** package code contains extensive unit/integration test declarations: core 314 in 20 files; client 541 in 63; server 862 in 82; Svelte 9 in 1; CLI 94 in 10; ExtFn 12 in 3; Swift bridge 25 in 5; Swift 50 `@Test` declarations in 14 files.

## External evidence gaps

* JavaScript/TypeScript build, lint, and 1,857 declared tests: **unverified** because no root/DataFn `node_modules` existed and installation was prohibited.
* Swift build/test and 50 declared tests: **unverified** because running SwiftPM would create `.build`, outside the authorized read-only implementation scope.
* Real Drizzle/Kysely/Prisma databases, transactions, uniqueness, concurrency, and retention: **unverified**.
* WebSocket HTTP upgrade auth and multi-process/multi-instance behavior: **unverified**.
* WKWebView origins, subframes, content worlds, navigation, and native credential handling: **unverified**.
* CloudKit entitlements, private database sync, account changes, conflicts, offline/reconnect, and device-to-device behavior: **unverified**.
* SearchFn native/JS package compatibility and large persistent indexes: **unverified**.
* Example applications, browser offline/hydration switches, extension runtime, and Svelte integration: **unverified**.
* npm/PyPI/Swift package publication, installability, license files, provenance, and registry availability: **unverified**.
* Docs build, links, code snippets, terminology audit, and search indexing: **unverified**; required `docs:audit` script is absent.
* Production metrics, SLOs, backup/restore, migration rollback, load/soak/fuzz testing, and vulnerability/dependency scanning: **unverified**.

## Recommendations (ranked)

 1. **Close trust-boundary blockers first:** DFA-001-DFA-004. Introduce one authorization context and one policy evaluator used by query/search/relations/sync/Swift bridge. Add adversarial omitted-select/wildcard/search/spoof/subframe tests.
 2. **Repair native sync correctness:** DFA-005-DFA-007. Use canonical server fixtures, paginated staged clone, partial acknowledgments, and an iCloud-native query adapter before enabling native release targets.
 3. **Unify canonical contracts:** DFA-008, DFA-009, DFA-012, DFA-018. Decide `$or` and bulk mutation support, then share fixtures/types across TS/Python/Swift.
 4. **Make writes transactionally truthful:** DFA-010-DFA-013 and DFA-026. Namespace/atomically claim idempotency, reject unsupported atomic requests, combine mutation/change/outbox, validate retention, and propagate storage failures.
 5. **Protect local data:** DFA-014-DFA-017 and DFA-019. Ship a restart-safe IndexedDB migration, staged clone readiness, ownership-safe context switching, and explicit Swift schema migration/compatibility.
 6. **Enforce scale caps:** DFA-020. Add group/changelog caps, remove full-result copies, batch relation work, push filtering to adapters, and run specified stress vectors.
 7. **Fix release gates:** DFA-021. Add Swift bridge to workspace/lock, Swift CI, docs audit, cross-runtime conformance, package metadata, clean-install/build/test/package dry-runs, and forbid silent conformance skips.
 8. **Remove global/ambiguous contracts:** DFA-022-DFA-024. Make SPv2 instance-scoped, resolve WebSocket precedence, and wrap adapters with DataFn schema plus namespace.
 9. **Harden deterministic/error semantics:** DFA-025-DFA-029. Inject clock/ID/order, fail on non-finite numbers and DB errors, authorize relation filter paths, scope privileged programmatic APIs, and reject codegen collisions.
10. **Finish lifecycle hygiene:** DFA-030 and operational tests for repeated create/close, timers, signals, storage reuse, process hooks, and shutdown.

Minimum release gate after fixes:

* clean install from lockfile;
* JS build/lint/typecheck/all tests with no skips for missing fixtures;
* Python tests across every declared supported Python version;
* Swift build/test on supported Apple platform plus bridge contract tests against the TS server;
* real SQL adapter transaction/concurrency suite;
* browser IndexedDB migration/offline/hydration suite;
* WKWebView adversarial origin/frame/navigation suite;
* CloudKit device/account/offline suite;
* docs audit/build/link/code validation;
* package dry-run/install from produced artifacts;
* migration forward/rollback and load/soak results attached to the release.

# Intent Audit (Coverage Mapping)

This document enumerates the intent items extracted from the authoritative audit section (2.1) and maps each item to spec coverage (SPEC.md sections, REQUIREMENTS.md IDs, and TEST_VECTORS.md vectors).

## Intent inventory (numbered)

1. Add a Clone Up / local-to-cloud upload capability to prevent data loss on local→cloud transition.
2. Support the offline-first signup flow (local data exists before cloud identity).
3. Upload ALL local persisted data by default; support an explicit subset of resources when requested.
4. Upload resource-by-resource (select all local records per resource; upload if non-empty).
5. Do not require a changelog→mutations conversion for clone up.
6. Ensure `clientId` is included and resource selection defaults to all when unspecified.
7. Provide a dedicated server endpoint `/datafn/cloneup` (rather than overloading `push`).
8. Ensure clone up is idempotent and safe to retry.

## Coverage mapping

| Intent ID | Source | Intent statement | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| INT-CLONEUP-001 | gap analysis 2.1 | Datafn must support Clone Up / local-to-cloud upload to prevent data loss when switching from local mode to cloud on signup. | SPEC.md (Overview, Goals), CLONEUP-001..005, CLONEUP-011, TV-CLONEUP-001/010 |
| INT-CLONEUP-002 | gap analysis 2.1 | Support offline-first signup flow: user creates data locally, then after signup uploads it to cloud. | SPEC.md (Overview, Context), CLONEUP-011, PHASE_03, TV-CLONEUP-010 |
| INT-CLONEUP-003 | gap analysis 2.1 | Upload ALL local persisted data by default; allow uploading a subset of resources when specified. | SPEC.md (Client → Resource selection), CLONEUP-011, CLONEUP-012, TV-CLONEUP-010/013 |
| INT-CLONEUP-004 | gap analysis 2.1 | Upload should be resource-by-resource: for each resource, select all local records and upload if any. | SPEC.md (Client semantics), CLONEUP-011/013, TV-CLONEUP-010 |
| INT-CLONEUP-005 | gap analysis 2.1 | Clone up must not require changelog → mutations conversion (push-only is insufficient). | SPEC.md (Non-goals + Client semantics), CLONEUP-011 |
| INT-CLONEUP-006 | gap analysis 2.1 | ClientId must be included; resources should be optional and default to all. | SPEC.md (CloneUpRequest + Client resource selection), CLONEUP-002/011/012, TV-CLONEUP-005/013 |
| INT-CLONEUP-007 | gap analysis 2.1 | Provide server endpoint `/datafn/cloneup` (or extend push); endpoint should exist and be callable by the client remote. | SPEC.md (Server HTTP API), CLONEUP-001/009/010, TV-CLONEUP-001/009 |
| INT-CLONEUP-008 | gap analysis 2.1 | Clone up must be idempotent and safe to retry in signup scenarios. | SPEC.md (Invariants → Idempotency), CLONEUP-004/005, TV-CLONEUP-003 |

## Non-goals audit

# Intent Audit (Coverage Mapping)

This audit maps every intent/finding from the user-provided audit observations plus repository scan findings to SPEC, REQUIREMENTS, and TEST_VECTORS coverage.

## Intent Inventory

1. Keep OAuth common infrastructure in shared packages (not per-function duplication).
2. Fix duplication in `oauth-testing` memory state/token stores.
3. Replace plugfn thin/memory-leaning OAuth wrapper path with production-ready persistent path.
4. Introduce a shared high-level OAuth flow package for common orchestration.
5. Migrate recfn calendar token storage/refresh from local interfaces to shared OAuth packages.
6. Extract reusable webhook signing/delivery utilities from recfn into shared packages.
7. Extract reusable response envelope helpers into shared packages.
8. Extract reusable error-code-to-HTTP-status mapping into shared packages.
9. Extract reusable queue adapter abstractions from recfn/cifn into shared packages.
10. Extract reusable metrics emitter interface from recfn into shared packages.
11. Extract reusable env/config loader patterns from recfn into shared packages.
12. Extract reusable bearer token auth middleware into shared auth package.
13. Unify rate limiting patterns (sliding window + token bucket) in shared package implementation.
14. Ensure OAuth scope includes redirect handling and webhooks-related reusable concerns where appropriate.

# Overview

This spec adds **Clone Up / Local-to-Cloud Upload** to Datafn so offline-first users who create data locally (before having a cloud identity) can **upload all existing local records to the cloud** after signup without data loss.

The feature introduces:

- A **server endpoint** `POST /datafn/cloneup` that accepts bulk records for a single resource and persists them with **change tracking**.
- A **client convenience method** `client.sync.cloneUpNow()` that reads all local records from configured storage and uploads them **resource-by-resource** (and chunked).

## Context

- **Project name:** Superfunctions monorepo (`datafn` packages)
- **One-sentence goal:** Implement Datafn “clone up” so local IndexedDB data can be uploaded to the cloud on signup.
- **Target users:** App developers migrating from Flux/Flux.ts patterns, and any offline-first app using `@datafn/client` + `@datafn/server`.
- **Target environments:**
  - Client: browser (IndexedDB) and Node (tests)
  - Server: Node 18+
- **Languages/packages:** TypeScript; `@datafn/client`, `@datafn/server`, `@datafn/core`, `@superfunctions/db`, `@superfunctions/http`
- **Existing systems to integrate with:**
  - Server auth/namespace isolation via `authContextProvider` (optional)
  - Server authorization callback `authorize()`
  - Server change tracking (`__datafn_meta`, `__datafn_changes`) and optional `SequenceStore`
- **Data model summary:**
  - User-defined resources (schema `resources`) keyed by `id`
  - Server global sequence (`serverSeq`) recorded per namespace in `__datafn_meta` and `__datafn_changes`
- **Security model:**
  - Per-request authorization via `DatafnServerConfig.authorize`
  - Optional per-user/tenant namespace via `authContextProvider` (affects where uploaded data is written)
- **Performance constraints:**
  - Must support large local datasets by chunking uploads and avoiding unnecessary writes
- **Hard constraints:**
  - No new external dependencies
  - Deterministic behavior for ordering, cursors, and error reporting

# Glossary

- **Local mode**: An app mode where data is written only to client storage (e.g., IndexedDB) prior to obtaining a cloud identity/session.
- **Clone down**: Download the full dataset from server to client (`/datafn/clone`).
- **Pull**: Incremental download of changes since a cursor (`/datafn/pull`).
- **Push**: Incremental upload of mutations from a client changelog (`/datafn/push`).
- **Clone up**: Bulk upload of existing local records to the server (this spec).
- **Resource**: A schema-defined table name (`DatafnSchema.resources[].name`).
- **Record**: A JSON object representing a resource row, MUST include string `id`.
- **Namespace**: A server-side partition key used for multi-user/tenant isolation of data and change tracking.
- **serverSeq**: Monotonic integer sequence allocated by the server for change tracking.
- **Cursor**: A base-10 integer string representing a `serverSeq` boundary.

# Goals / Non-goals

## Goals

1. Datafn MUST support uploading all local records to the server after a user transitions from local/offline mode to cloud mode.
2. Clone up MUST support **resource-by-resource** uploads (matching Flux’s workflow) and MUST be chunkable.
3. Server-side clone up MUST record change tracking so other clients can pull the uploaded records.
4. Clone up MUST be **idempotent by content**: repeating the same upload MUST NOT generate additional change tracking entries for unchanged records.

## Non-goals

1. This spec does not change `push()` semantics (incremental mutation upload remains unchanged).
2. This spec does not add reconciliation, pagination workflows, KV store patterns, or in-memory store patterns.
3. This spec does not define a new cross-resource transaction primitive for clone up; uploads are per-resource and may partially succeed.

# Public API

## Server HTTP API

### Endpoint

- **Method/Path**: `POST /datafn/cloneup`
- **Content-Type**: `application/json`
- **Response envelope**: `DatafnEnvelope<CloneUpResult>`

### Request: `CloneUpRequest`

```ts
export type CloneUpRequest = {
  clientId: string;
  resource: string;
  records: Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
};
```

### Result: `CloneUpResult`

```ts
export type CloneUpResult = {
  ok: true;
  resource: string;
  inserted: string[];
  updated: string[];
  skipped: string[];
  errors: Array<{
    id: string;
    code: string;
    message: string;
    path: string;
  }>;
  cursor: string; // base-10 integer string
};
```

Notes:

- Request-level validation failures MUST return `{ ok: false, error: ... }` with an appropriate HTTP status (typically 400).
- Record-level failures MUST be reported in `errors[]` while allowing other records to proceed.

## Client TypeScript API (`@datafn/client`)

### Remote adapter

```ts
export interface DatafnRemoteAdapter {
  // existing
  seed(payload: unknown): Promise<unknown>;
  clone(payload: unknown): Promise<unknown>;
  pull(payload: unknown): Promise<unknown>;
  push(payload: unknown): Promise<unknown>;

  // new
  cloneUp(payload: unknown): Promise<unknown>;
}
```

### Sync facade (delegating method)

```ts
export interface SyncFacade {
  // existing
  seed(payload: unknown): Promise<unknown>;
  clone(payload: unknown): Promise<unknown>;
  pull(payload: unknown): Promise<unknown>;
  push(payload: unknown): Promise<unknown>;

  // new (delegates to remote.cloneUp)
  cloneUp(payload: unknown): Promise<unknown>;
}
```

### Sync convenience method (local-to-cloud)

`createDatafnClient()` MUST expose an additional method on `client.sync`:

```ts
export type CloneUpNowOptions = {
  /** If omitted, upload all schema resources (including isRemoteOnly). */
  resources?: string[];
  /** Max records per request. Default: 500. */
  batchSize?: number;
};

export type CloneUpNowSummary = {
  ok: boolean; // true iff no per-record errors occurred
  cursor: string; // max cursor observed across all cloneup calls (or current cursor if no writes)
  resources: Array<{
    resource: string;
    inserted: string[];
    updated: string[];
    skipped: string[];
    errors: CloneUpResult["errors"];
  }>;
};

// new method
client.sync.cloneUpNow(options?: CloneUpNowOptions): Promise<CloneUpNowSummary>;
```

## Plugin hook API (`@datafn/core`)

`DatafnPlugin.beforeSync` / `afterSync` MUST accept the additional phase:

```ts
type SyncPhase = "seed" | "clone" | "pull" | "push" | "cloneup";
```

# Data formats / protocol

## Envelope

All server responses MUST conform to `DatafnEnvelope<T>`:

```ts
type DatafnEnvelope<T> =
  | { ok: true; result: T }
  | { ok: false; error: { code: string; message: string; details?: unknown } };
```

## Canonical clone up request/response

### Request JSON

```json
{
  "clientId": "client:device-1",
  "resource": "task",
  "records": [
    { "id": "task:1", "title": "a" },
    { "id": "task:2", "title": "b" }
  ]
}
```

### Success response JSON

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "result": {
    "ok": true,
    "resource": "task",
    "inserted": ["task:1", "task:2"],
    "updated": [],
    "skipped": [],
    "errors": [],
    "cursor": "2"
  }
}
```

### Request-level error response JSON

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "DFQL_INVALID",
    "message": "Invalid DFQL: clientId must be string",
    "details": { "path": "clientId" }
  }
}
```

# Semantics

## Server: `/datafn/cloneup`

### Validation

The server MUST validate, in order:

1. `clientId` MUST be a string.
2. `resource` MUST be a string and MUST exist in `DatafnSchema.resources`.
3. `records` MUST be an array.
4. Each `records[i]` MUST be an object (non-null, not an array) and MUST include `id: string`.
5. If the resource schema defines `idPrefix`, then `record.id` MUST start with that prefix.
6. Each record’s keys MUST be valid writable fields for that resource per server schema validation rules.

Request-level validation failures MUST return envelope error (`ok: false`) and MUST NOT partially apply any writes.

### Persistence + change tracking

For each valid record:

- The server MUST apply **upsert semantics**:
  - If the record does not exist: `create` it.
  - If the record exists: `update` it using **merge semantics** (only the provided keys).
- The server MUST record a change tracking entry **only if** the upsert changes persisted content.
  - If the existing record already matches the incoming record for all provided keys, the server MUST treat it as `skipped` and MUST NOT record a change.

The server MUST allocate `serverSeq` using `ChangeTrackingService.getNextServerSeq()` for each recorded change, and MUST return `cursor` as the maximum `serverSeq` recorded during this request, or the current global `serverSeq` if no changes were recorded.

### Partial failures

- If a specific record fails validation (e.g., unknown field) the server MUST report it in `errors[]` and continue processing remaining records.
- If a database operation fails for a specific record, the server MUST report it in `errors[]` with `code: "INTERNAL"` and continue processing remaining records.

## Client: `client.sync.cloneUpNow()`

### Preconditions

- The client MUST have a configured `storage` adapter.
- The client MUST have a configured `sync.remote` (i.e., a remote adapter that implements `cloneUp`).

If these are not met, `cloneUpNow()` MUST throw a deterministic `DatafnClientError`:

- Missing storage → `DFQL_INVALID` with `details.path = "storage"`.
- Missing remote cloneUp method → `TRANSPORT_ERROR` with `details.path = "sync.cloneUp"`.

### Resource selection

- If `options.resources` is provided, the client MUST upload only those resources, in the given order.
- Otherwise, the client MUST upload all schema resources in schema order, including those marked `isRemoteOnly`.

### Record selection + ordering

For each selected resource:

1. Read all local records via `storage.listRecords(resource)`.
2. If zero records, skip remote call for that resource.
3. Sort records by `id` ascending (lexicographic) for determinism.
4. Chunk into batches of at most `options.batchSize` (default 500) and call `/datafn/cloneup` once per batch.

### Aggregation

The client MUST aggregate per-batch results into a per-resource summary, concatenating `inserted/updated/skipped` arrays in the order batches were sent.

The client MUST compute `summary.cursor` as the maximum numeric cursor returned by any batch result (or the current stored cursor if no batches ran).

# Invariants

## Determinism

- Given the same request payload and server state, `/datafn/cloneup` MUST produce the same `inserted/updated/skipped/errors` partitioning and MUST allocate `serverSeq` in a deterministic order (processing records sorted by `id`).
- Error ordering MUST be deterministic: errors MUST be listed in ascending record `id` order within the request.

## Idempotency

- Repeating the same clone up request (same `resource`, same set of records and values) MUST NOT create additional change tracking entries for unchanged records.
- A partially successful request MAY be retried; already-applied identical records MUST be skipped.

## Ordering

- Within a request, record processing order MUST be `id` ascending.
- Across client resources, processing order MUST match the client’s resource iteration order.

# Security

## Authorization

- `DatafnServerConfig.authorize` MUST support the new action string `"cloneup"`.
- Authorization MUST run only after JSON parsing succeeds (consistent with existing `withAuth`).

## Namespace isolation

- The clone up endpoint MUST write records to the namespace returned by `authContextProvider` when configured; otherwise it MUST use the default namespace (`"datafn"`).

## Validation

- The server MUST validate unknown resources/fields and reject or report deterministically.
- The server MUST NOT log record bodies.

# Limits / caps

- The server MAY enforce request payload limits via `limits.maxPayloadBytes` (existing middleware).
- The client MUST provide chunking (default 500 records per request) to keep payload sizes bounded.

# Observability

- The server MUST log a structured `logRequest` entry for `/datafn/cloneup` including: timestamp, endpoint, operation="cloneup", clientId, resource, count, duration_ms.
- Errors MUST be surfaced only via response envelopes and MUST NOT include sensitive record contents.

# Compatibility / versioning strategy

- This change is additive:
  - Adds a new endpoint (`/datafn/cloneup`).
  - Extends types to include a new sync phase and new remote method.
- Existing endpoints (`clone`, `pull`, `push`, `seed`) MUST remain behaviorally unchanged.

# Undefined / Explicitly user-deferred only

None.

### ID: CLONEUP-001

- **Priority:** P0
- **Statement:** The server MUST expose `POST /datafn/cloneup` that returns a `DatafnEnvelope<CloneUpResult>`.
- **Rationale:** Datafn lacks the Flux `cloneUp()` capability; this endpoint is the server-side primitive for local-to-cloud upload.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - A request matching `CloneUpRequest` returns HTTP 200 with `{ ok: true, result: { ok: true, ... } }`.
  - Invalid request-level inputs return `{ ok: false, error: ... }` with a non-2xx status.
- **Test vectors:** TV-CLONEUP-001, TV-CLONEUP-005
- **Notes:** Endpoint path is appended to client `sync.remote` base URL (e.g., `${baseUrl}/cloneup`).

### ID: CLONEUP-002

- **Priority:** P0
- **Statement:** The server MUST reject invalid request-level fields (`clientId`, `resource`, `records`) with an envelope error and MUST NOT apply any writes.
- **Rationale:** Request-level validation failures are unrecoverable for safe partial execution and must fail deterministically.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Missing or non-string `clientId` returns `DFQL_INVALID` with `details.path = "clientId"`.
  - Unknown `resource` returns `DFQL_UNKNOWN_RESOURCE` with `details.path = "resource"`.
  - Non-array `records` returns `DFQL_INVALID` with `details.path = "records"`.
  - For any of the above failures, no records are created/updated in the database.
- **Test vectors:** TV-CLONEUP-001 (positive), TV-CLONEUP-005, TV-CLONEUP-006
- **Notes:** This is distinct from per-record failures (CLONEUP-003).

### ID: CLONEUP-003

- **Priority:** P0
- **Statement:** The server MUST validate records individually and MUST report invalid records in `CloneUpResult.errors[]` while continuing to process other valid records.
- **Rationale:** Local datasets may contain a small number of malformed rows; clone up should salvage remaining user data.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - A record that is not an object is reported as an error with a deterministic `path` referencing `records[i]`.
  - A record missing `id: string` is reported as an error and is not written.
  - A record containing unknown fields is reported as an error and is not written.
  - Valid records in the same request are still inserted/updated.
- **Test vectors:** TV-CLONEUP-002 (positive), TV-CLONEUP-005 (negative control: request-level failure stops all)
- **Notes:** Error ordering MUST be deterministic (SPEC.md → Invariants → Determinism).

### ID: CLONEUP-005

- **Priority:** P0
- **Statement:** The server MUST return `cursor` as a base-10 integer string representing the latest `serverSeq` observed after processing the request.
- **Rationale:** The client and other clients need a stable cursor boundary for subsequent pulls.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - If at least one change is recorded, `cursor` equals the maximum allocated `serverSeq` for this request.
  - If no changes are recorded, `cursor` equals the current global `serverSeq` for the namespace.
  - `cursor` matches `/^\d+$/`.
- **Test vectors:** TV-CLONEUP-001 (positive), TV-CLONEUP-003 (positive+negative), TV-CLONEUP-005 (negative request-level)
- **Notes:** Cursor semantics match `/datafn/push` (global cursor).

### ID: CLONEUP-006

- **Priority:** P1
- **Statement:** The server MUST write clone up data into the namespace derived from `authContextProvider` when configured, otherwise into the default namespace `"datafn"`.
- **Rationale:** Clone up must respect multi-user/multi-tenant isolation, or it will leak data across identities.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - When `authContextProvider` returns `userId`, clone up writes are isolated to that user namespace.
  - When `authContextProvider` is absent, clone up writes go to `"datafn"`.
- **Test vectors:** TV-CLONEUP-001 (default namespace), TV-CLONEUP-012 (namespace isolation)
- **Notes:** TV-CLONEUP-012 is a multi-step test that creates two contexts and ensures isolation.

### ID: CLONEUP-007

- **Priority:** P1
- **Statement:** Server plugins MUST receive `beforeSync/afterSync` callbacks for clone up as `phase = "cloneup"`.
- **Rationale:** Sync hooks are part of the server extension model; clone up must be observable and interceptable.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - A `beforeSync` hook can transform clone up payload.
  - A throwing/rejecting `beforeSync` hook rejects the request with an envelope error.
  - An `afterSync` hook runs after successful execution.
- **Test vectors:** TV-CLONEUP-007
- **Notes:** Hook runner semantics must remain consistent (fail-closed before, fail-open after).

### ID: CLONEUP-008

- **Priority:** P1
- **Statement:** `DatafnServerConfig.authorize` MUST accept the action `"cloneup"` and MUST be invoked after successful JSON parsing.
- **Rationale:** Authorization must cover all endpoints uniformly and must not mask parse errors.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Invalid JSON returns `DFQL_INVALID` without calling `authorize`.
  - When `authorize` returns false, server responds with HTTP 403 and `{ ok: false, error: { code: "FORBIDDEN", ... } }`.
- **Test vectors:** TV-CLONEUP-001 (positive allow), TV-CLONEUP-008 (negative deny)
- **Notes:** Mirrors AUTH-001 behavior already implemented for other endpoints.

- **Priority:** P0

- **Rationale:** The client needs a transport-level entry point for the new endpoint.

- **Priority:** P0
- **Statement:** `@datafn/client` MUST extend `SyncFacade` with `cloneUp(payload)` that delegates to `remote.cloneUp` and unwraps envelopes.
- **Rationale:** SyncFacade is the existing delegation surface for sync methods; clone up should be available there.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - `client.sync.cloneUp(payload)` calls `remote.cloneUp(payload)`.
  - If the server returns `{ ok: false, error: ... }`, the client throws a `DatafnClientError`.
- **Test vectors:** TV-CLONEUP-009

### ID: CLONEUP-011

- **Priority:** P0
- **Statement:** `@datafn/client` MUST implement `client.sync.cloneUpNow()` to upload all existing local records to the server without requiring a changelog-to-mutation conversion.

### ID: OAUTH-001

- **Priority:** P0
- **Statement:** `@superfunctions/oauth-testing` MUST re-export in-memory state/token stores from `@superfunctions/oauth-storage` instead of maintaining duplicate implementations.
- **Rationale:** Duplicate memory store logic has already diverged and increases maintenance and bug risk.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - `packages/oauth-testing/src/index.ts` imports and re-exports memory stores from `@superfunctions/oauth-storage`.
  - No local `Map`-backed store class definitions remain in oauth-testing.
  - Existing oauth-testing tests continue to pass with unchanged runtime behavior.
- **Test vectors:** TV-OAUTH-001-P, TV-OAUTH-001-N
- **Notes:** Backward-compatible export names MUST remain available.

### ID: OAUTH-002

- **Priority:** P0
- **Statement:** A new `@superfunctions/oauth-flow` package MUST provide a high-level OAuth orchestration service API that composes oauth-core/oauth-http/oauth-storage.
- **Rationale:** authfn and plugfn currently duplicate orchestration responsibilities with different behaviors.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - `packages/oauth-flow` exists with typed public API and tests.
  - Service exposes start/callback/refresh/disconnect methods.
  - Package has no framework-specific runtime dependency.
- **Test vectors:** TV-OAUTH-002-P, TV-OAUTH-002-N
- **Notes:** Package must remain composable for both authfn and plugfn identity models.

### ID: OAUTH-003

- **Priority:** P0
- **Statement:** `oauth-flow.start()` MUST enforce provider existence, redirect allowlist validation, PKCE generation, and state persistence with TTL.
- **Rationale:** Start-step validation and PKCE consistency are critical for secure OAuth initiation.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Unknown provider returns deterministic validation error.
  - Disallowed redirect URI is rejected before state creation.
  - PKCE challenge/method are included when provider supports PKCE.
  - State record includes expiry timestamp and subject identifiers.
- **Test vectors:** TV-OAUTH-003-P, TV-OAUTH-003-N
- **Notes:** TTL default should align with existing oauth-core defaults unless explicitly overridden.

### ID: OAUTH-004

- **Priority:** P0
- **Statement:** `oauth-flow.handleCallback()` MUST atomically consume state and reject replay, expiry, provider mismatch, and redirect mismatch with deterministic error codes.
- **Rationale:** Replay and callback mismatch protections are core OAuth invariants.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - First valid callback succeeds.
  - Replayed callback for same state returns replay error code.
  - Mismatched redirect/provider callback returns mismatch error code.
  - Expired state returns invalid/expired error code.
- **Test vectors:** TV-OAUTH-004-P, TV-OAUTH-004-N
- **Notes:** Callback processing must not leak token material in error details.

### ID: OAUTH-005

- **Priority:** P0
- **Statement:** `oauth-flow.refresh()` MUST preserve existing refresh tokens when providers omit a replacement and MUST update encrypted token records deterministically.
- **Rationale:** Some providers do not rotate refresh tokens every refresh response.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Successful refresh updates access token and expiry metadata.
  - Missing new refresh token keeps prior refresh token value.
  - Refresh failure leaves prior token record intact.
- **Test vectors:** TV-OAUTH-005-P, TV-OAUTH-005-N
- **Notes:** Deterministic update timestamps are required for auditability.

### ID: OAUTH-006

- **Priority:** P0
- **Statement:** `oauth-flow.disconnect()` MUST perform local token/connection cleanup even when remote revoke fails.
- **Rationale:** Local credential lifecycle must not depend on remote provider availability.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Successful remote revoke produces full cleanup result.
  - Remote revoke failure still deletes local token and connection records.
  - Result surface includes attempted/cleanup flags.
- **Test vectors:** TV-OAUTH-006-P, TV-OAUTH-006-N
- **Notes:** Failure should be surfaced after cleanup, not before.

- **Priority:** P1

# Overview

## Project context

- **Project name**: Superfunctions root docs
- **One-sentence goal**: Rebuild the root `docs/` site into a beginner-first, category-organized, external-facing documentation experience that explains the Superfunctions mission and ecosystem and thoroughly documents every shared package.
- **Target users**:
  - External library authors evaluating `@superfunctions/*` and Python shared packages
  - Application engineers deciding which Superfunctions packages to compose
  - Contributors who need a public-facing explanation of package scope without internal monorepo context
- **Target environments**:
  - Static docs rendered in the existing Next.js + Fumadocs root docs app
  - Desktop and mobile web browsers
  - Local docs development via `npm -w docs run dev`
- **Languages/packages required**:
  - MDX under `docs/content/docs`
  - TypeScript/JavaScript for docs layout and verification scripts
  - Existing shared packages under `packages/*` and `packages/python-*`
- **Existing systems it must integrate with**:
  - Current root docs app in `docs/`
  - `@superfunctions/docs-theme`
  - Fumadocs page tree generation from `meta.json`
  - Existing package README files and package metadata as canonical technical source material
- **Data model summary**:
  - A docs page tree
  - A machine-readable shared-package catalog
  - A machine-readable ecosystem catalog
  - Deterministic docs quality-check results emitted as JSON from local scripts
- **Security model**:
  - Public docs only; no auth required
  - No secrets, internal-only runbooks, private URLs, or unpublished migration/deprecation guidance in user-facing root docs
- **Performance constraints**:
  - `npm -w docs run build` MUST remain successful locally
  - Docs verification scripts MUST complete in local development without external services
  - Content-quality checks SHOULD be deterministic and fast enough for pre-commit or local repeated runs
- **Non-goals / out of scope**:
  - Rewriting dedicated docs apps for `datafn`, `searchfn`, `hostfn`, or other top-level functions
  - Changing package APIs or renaming packages
  - Publishing/versioning the docs site
  - Adding internationalization, docs search tuning, or analytics
- **Hard constraints**:
  - Keep the existing root docs workspace and Fumadocs stack
  - Treat the site as an external/public docs surface, not an internal implementation notebook
  - No migration, legacy, deprecation, or release-note sections in root docs navigation or package pages
  - Use real package names and real imports only

The current root docs pass structural checks while still reading like placeholders. The site title, landing page, sidebar labels, package grouping, and most package pages are written as if they are internal scaffolding. This spec fixes the information architecture, content contract, and local quality gates so that the docs become useful to first-time external readers.

# Glossary

- **Root docs site**: The `docs/` workspace at the repo root that documents the Superfunctions ecosystem and the reusable shared packages.
- **Shared package**: A reusable package under `packages/*` or `packages/python-*` intended for composition across multiple Superfunctions and by external consumers.
- **Primitive package**: A low-level shared package such as `@superfunctions/http`, `@superfunctions/db`, or `@superfunctions/envelope`.
- **Category overview page**: A landing page for one user-facing package group such as Authentication & OAuth or Data & Storage.
- **Package page**: A single docs page for one shared package or Python integration package.
- **Start Here section**: The root onboarding group containing the introduction, getting-started, package chooser, and ecosystem pages.
- **Ecosystem catalog**: A machine-readable list of top-level Superfunctions and where readers should go next for their docs.
- **Package catalog**: A machine-readable list of shared-package docs entries, categories, ordering, and content requirements.
- **External library author**: A developer building their own package, SDK, or service on top of Superfunctions shared packages.
- **Placeholder copy**: Generic prose that does not explain real behavior, tradeoffs, or usage. Examples include “Reference and usage guidance” and fake production examples with no executable substance.

# Goals / Non-goals

## Goals

1. The root docs MUST explain what Superfunctions is, who the root docs are for, and how the ecosystem fits together.
2. The sidebar MUST be reorganized by beginner-friendly package categories instead of “Shared” buckets.
3. Every shared package page MUST be rewritten with thorough, real, external-world-oriented content.
4. The root docs MUST link readers to the broader Superfunctions ecosystem, including top-level function docs entry points.
5. The docs MUST stop surfacing migrations, legacy notes, deprecations, and release-note content in this root site.
6. Local verification MUST block the current class of “technically present but content-thin” placeholder pages.

## Non-goals

1. This spec does not require a new docs framework or a new root app.
2. This spec does not create or rewrite dedicated docs products for each function package.
3. This spec does not add versioned docs, migration guides, deprecation policy docs, or release-note feeds.

export type DocsCheckErrorCode =

# Glossary

- **PlugFn provider**: A reusable integration adapter exposing named actions and webhook triggers behind PlugFn's core runtime.
- **Ready package**: A shared package already classified as sufficient for Conduct v0.3.0, subject only to compatibility verification.
- **CliFn**: A reusable CLI primitives runtime for credentials, project config, HTTP client behavior, UI, stdio, and prompts.
- **Dependency harness**: A focused integration test/example proving that a shared package satisfies Conduct's needs without forking or ad hoc patches.
- **Direct Drizzle fallback**: A schema definition path used when `@superfunctions/cli` code generation cannot yet express a required constraint or composite index.
- **Provider trigger**: A verified webhook event exposed by a PlugFn provider to downstream consumers.

# Goals / Non-goals

## Goals

1. Superfunctions MUST provide every reusable package capability that Conduct v0.3.0 depends on.

# Semantics

## PlugFn as the integration runtime

Superfunctions MUST supply provider actions and triggers through PlugFn rather than introducing a Conduct-specific integration subsystem. Provider implementations stay reusable and only expose generic actions/triggers; Conduct owns workflow orchestration and state mapping.

## `clifn` extraction strategy

Conduct may prove APIs inline first, but the superfunctions dependency outcome for v0.3.0 is a reusable `clifn` package with stable subpath exports for credentials, config, client, UI, stdio, and prompt helpers.

## Ready-package validation

`@superfunctions/db`, `@superfunctions/storage-s3`, `@superfunctions/webhooks`, `@superfunctions/queue`, `@superfunctions/http`, `@superfunctions/auth`, `@superfunctions/config`, `@superfunctions/errors`, `@superfunctions/envelope`, and `@superfunctions/middleware` remain unchanged unless dependency harnesses prove otherwise. Conduct MUST consume them through their existing public APIs.

## Schema-generation gap handling

Conduct's schema needs composite indexes and CHECK constraints. Superfunctions MUST support that requirement either by extending `@superfunctions/cli` generation or by documenting and testing a direct Drizzle fallback so the gap never blocks Conduct.

## Package placement and workspace rules

New dependency work MUST follow repo conventions:

- `clifn` lives as a normal top-level function package with a subpackage workspace.
- workspaces are updated in root `package.json`.
- no nested monorepos are introduced.
- package names remain unscoped for function packages and `@superfunctions/*` for shared packages.

# Invariants

1. PlugFn providers MUST remain Conduct-agnostic and reusable by other consumers.
2. Provider action and trigger names listed in this spec are stable public contracts once shipped.
3. Provider webhook triggers MUST verify signatures before emitting events.
4. `clifn` public subpaths MUST stay deterministic and usable in non-Conduct CLIs.
5. Ready packages MUST NOT be changed speculatively without a failing harness or explicit gap proof.
6. Secrets MUST NOT be echoed by `clifn` UI or test fixtures.

# Security

- PlugFn OAuth tokens and webhook secrets remain inside provider/runtime layers and MUST NOT be exposed through Conduct-specific helper code.
- `clifn` credential storage MUST read/write local profile files without printing secret values in styled output.
- Provider webhook tests MUST cover signature failures as negative cases.
- No dependency package in this spec may require Conduct to handle raw PM credentials directly.

# Limits/caps

- Linear issue search defaults to `first=20` unless the caller overrides it.
- `clifn` stdin/stdout helpers MUST operate on single JSON documents and MUST fail fast on invalid JSON.
- Provider compatibility tests MUST run locally without live third-party network calls.
- ClickUp provider pagination defaults MAY follow provider norms, but task listing MUST be cursor- or page-token-safe and deterministic.

# Observability

Superfunctions dependency work MUST provide:

- unit tests for new provider actions and triggers
- fixture-backed webhook verification tests
- `clifn` tests for credentials, config, client retries, stdio, and prompts
- example usage in READMEs or provider docs for the new actions

Superfunctions dependency work MUST NOT:

- emit secret-bearing test snapshots
- rely on opaque manual verification for provider contract changes

# Compatibility / versioning strategy

- New provider capabilities are additive and should ship as backward-compatible minor releases unless a package's existing contract must change.
- `clifn` starts as a new package and MUST publish stable subpath exports from its first release.
- Conduct-facing examples in docs MUST use only public shared-package APIs.

# Undefined / Explicitly user-deferred only

- DataFn adoption for Conduct memory/query semantics.
- Full Slack interaction-platform support inside PlugFn unless a later dependency audit requires it.
- Changes to package families not referenced by the Conduct dependency audit.

# Architecture sketch

- `plugfn/typescript/src/providers/linear/*` gains additional actions and verified webhook triggers for Conduct-compatible Linear workflows.
- `plugfn/typescript/src/providers/github/*` gains issue update/read plus PR/review capabilities and comment/closure triggers.
- `plugfn/typescript/src/providers/clickup/*` is added as a new provider package/module following existing provider patterns.

# Plan

## Architecture sketch

### Docs structure

1. Keep the existing `docs/` Next.js + Fumadocs workspace.
2. Replace the current `shared`, `shared-packages`, `migrations`, and release-note-centric grouping with a category-driven docs tree.
3. Add two machine-readable sources:
   - `docs/lib/package-catalog.ts`
   - `docs/lib/ecosystem-catalog.ts`
4. Drive validation from those catalogs so nav, coverage, and content depth stay aligned.

### Content model

1. `Start Here` pages:
   - `index.mdx`
   - `getting-started.mdx`
   - `choosing-packages.mdx`
   - `ecosystem.mdx`
2. Category overview pages:
   - `authentication/index.mdx`
   - `http/index.mdx`
   - `middleware-runtime/index.mdx`
   - `data-storage/index.mdx`
   - `python/index.mdx`
   - `tooling/index.mdx`
3. Package pages grouped beneath those categories.

### Validation model

1. `check:catalog`
   - validates category coverage, order, and catalog completeness
2. `check:content`
   - validates required pages, required headings, page depth, banned phrases, and example validity
3. `check:snippets`
   - validates real package imports in fenced code blocks
4. `check:links`
   - validates internal docs routes

## Dependency graph

1. Catalog design comes first:
   - category taxonomy
   - package-to-category mapping
   - ecosystem link catalog
2. Start Here pages depend on:
   - final site identity
   - ecosystem catalog
3. Category overview pages depend on:
   - package catalog
   - final sidebar grouping
4. Package page rewrites depend on:
   - category structure
   - canonical README/source material
5. Final QA depends on:
   - complete page set
   - integrated scripts in `docs/package.json`

## Phases overview

| Phase | Goal | Delivered capability | Verification method |
|---|---|---|---|
| 00 | Define catalogs and docs contract | machine-readable package/ecosystem mapping + QA script scaffolding | `npm -w docs run check:catalog` |
| 01 | Rebrand and reframe the root site | site title + Start Here pages + ecosystem framing | `npm -w docs run build` + manual sidebar review |
| 02 | Implement Authentication & OAuth docs group | category overview + full auth/oauth package docs | `npm -w docs run check:content` |
| 03 | Implement HTTP docs group | category overview + core HTTP + adapter pages | `npm -w docs run check:content` |
| 04 | Implement Middleware & Runtime docs group | overview + middleware/runtime package docs | `npm -w docs run check:content` |
| 05 | Implement Data & Storage docs group | overview + db/storage/files package docs | `npm -w docs run check:content` |
| 06 | Implement Python + Tooling docs groups | overview + Python integration pages + tooling pages | `npm -w docs run check:content` |
| 07 | Remove irrelevant legacy docs surfaces and finalize QA | cleaned nav/routes + full local verification suite passing | full docs verification suite |

## Definition of Done

No phase is complete unless its verification steps pass.

The spec is complete only when:

1. All P0 requirements pass their referenced test vectors.
2. The sidebar no longer exposes `Shared Packages`, `migrations`, or release-note/deprecation sections.
3. Every shared package page satisfies the required page contract and content-depth rules.
4. The ecosystem page covers every top-level function in scope.
5. `npm -w docs run build`, `check:catalog`, `check:content`, `check:snippets`, and `check:links` all pass locally.
