arguments.content:
# SearchFn production-readiness audit

## Metadata

- Audit date: 2026-08-11
- Auditor: `audit_api_search`
- Model: GPT-5 (Codex)
- Launcher: Codex Desktop
- Repository state: detached `HEAD` at `721eefdd9cd716894e5329123a9e2fb615783611`
- Scope root: `searchfn/`, plus SearchFn-specific workflow/scripts and directly referenced DataFn integration files needed to assess SearchFn's migration contract.
- Method: independent, read-only source and specification review. Existing SearchFn audit conclusions were not used as compliance evidence.
- Evidence labels:
  - **Directly verified**: observed at the pinned commit or emitted by a read-only command in this audit.
  - **Static**: inferred from source/configuration; the corresponding runtime was not executed.
  - **Unverified**: requires build, package, platform, registry, browser, CI, or external-service execution that was not performed.
- Overall decision: **NO-GO for production**. Cross-tenant/resource identifier collisions, authorization/validation bypasses, backend error disclosure, false readiness, persistence consistency defects, and release/QA gaps are blockers.

## Audit scope

The audit covers every SearchFn product surface present at the pinned revision:

- Canonical contracts, core engine, WebAssembly/Rust engine, client and server.
- Memory, IndexedDB, PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, and Meilisearch adapters.
- DataFn provider bridge and the directly referenced DataFn client migration surface.
- Legacy aggregate `searchfn/adapters` compatibility area and its canonical-source guard.
- Swift package, SQLite/memory adapters, convenience API, examples, and tests.
- Python package/server/indexing/search implementation and tests.
- Docs site/Fumadocs content, migration/design documents, examples, benchmarks, package manifests, build/test/export metadata, release notes, and CI workflows.
- Five complete spec bundles, including every principal document, phase plan, phase report, and auxiliary inventory/export mapping.

The static inventory contains **418 regular files** under `searchfn/` after excluding generated/dependency directories, plus one tracked dangling symlink. Major areas are `.conduct` (132), core (47), docs (41), client (28), adapters/compatibility (25), Swift (24), server (15), PostgreSQL (15), Meilisearch (14), core-wasm (13), Elasticsearch (13), IndexedDB (10), memory (9), OpenSearch (9), Python (8), DataFn provider (7), and adapter contracts (6). Forty-four test-related files and approximately 416 `it`/`test` declarations were found by static search; no runtime pass claim is implied.

The tracked `searchfn/AGENTS.md` is an absolute, machine-specific symlink whose target is absent in this checkout. Its contents could not be read. Repository-root `AGENTS.md` governed this audit. The dangling link is itself reported as SEARCHFN-014.

## Inputs audited (intent + spec bundles)

### Product intent/design/documentation

- `searchfn/.conduct/spec.md`
- `searchfn/.conduct/searchfn-rust-engine-design.md`
- `searchfn/.conduct/canonical-source-policy.md`
- `searchfn/.conduct/migration/searchfn-rewrite-inventory.md`
- `searchfn/CHANGELOG.md`
- All package READMEs, Swift/Python documentation and examples, Fumadocs pages, API/operations/adapter guides, benchmarks, and migration material under `searchfn/`.

### Complete specification-bundle inventory

| Bundle | Intent statements | Requirement occurrences | Phase plans | Phase reports | Notable auxiliary inputs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `2026-03-08-new-97a4c153-spec` | 16 | 27 | 11 | 11 | Client/server rewrite, adapters, docs, production readiness |
| `2026-03-08-new-q4k7m2r8-spec` | 30 | 43 | 7 | 7 | Core/adapters, DataFn integration, compatibility, limits |
| `2026-03-11-new-h3r9k2m7-spec` | 7 | 12 | 7 | 7 | Package split; phase-00 inventory and export mapping |
| `2026-03-12-change-p7x3k9m2-spec` | 16 | 22 | 4 | 4 | Prefix/defaults/capability change |
| `2026-03-28-new-s7k4m2p9-spec` | 9 | 10 | 6 | 6 | Swift local/in-process architecture |
| **Total** | **78** | **114** | **35** | **35** | Principal `INTENT_AUDIT`, `SPEC`, `REQUIREMENTS`, `TEST_VECTORS`, `PLAN`, and log files inspected for each bundle |

Requirement counts are occurrences because IDs such as `API-001` and `MIG-001` are reused with different meanings in separate bundles. Coverage is therefore reported per bundle, never merged by the bare ID.

### Runtime, packaging, and verification inputs

- All `src/`, Rust, Swift, Python, tests, fixtures, examples, scripts, package manifests, `tsup`/TypeScript/Vitest/Swift/Python configs, docs configuration, benchmarks, and SearchFn workflow YAML.
- Commands used: pinned revision/status checks; `find`, `rg`, and `jq` inventories; manifest/export/script inspection; requirement parsing; `node scripts/check-searchfn-adapter-canonical.mjs`.
- Not run: dependency installation, builds, typechecking, lint, package test suites, Cargo/Swift/Python tests, Docker integration matrix, docs build, package pack/publish, browser checks, external databases/search engines, or CI.

## High-level findings

| Severity | Count | Headline |
|---|---:|---|
| Critical | 1 | Resource-name and document-ID normalization collide across tenants/resources and adapters. |
| High | 8 | Authorization can see a different payload than handlers; backend errors leak; readiness is sticky/false; IndexedDB/Swift/Python consistency and distribution/QA are not production-grade. |
| Medium | 5 | Meilisearch semantics, external-adapter bounds, deterministic provider behavior, conflicting bundles/legacy aggregate, and portable local instructions remain unresolved. |

Coverage verdict across **114 requirement occurrences**: **68 PASS, 27 PARTIAL, 19 FAIL, 0 UNVERIFIED**. These are static implementation statuses. External-service/platform/package acceptance remains unverified even when a requirement is marked PASS.

## Spec conflicts / spec gaps

1. **Compatibility policy has no precedence.** The 97a bundle says to spend no effort on backward compatibility and remove legacy code; q4 mandates `InMemorySearchFn`, core/advanced API, export, and DataFn migration compatibility. h3 authorizes destruction of the aggregate, while `canonical-source-policy.md:1-30` requires compatibility wrappers. No decision record says which source wins.
2. **The aggregate's declared removal did not occur cleanly.** `searchfn/adapters` still contains source, tests, benchmarks, and scripts. `searchfn/CHANGELOG.md:3-39` says the aggregate was removed/replaced while placeholder/compatibility material remains.
3. **Prefix semantics assume incorrect Meili behavior.** p7 requires native prefix support/capability and construct defaults, but `searchfn/adapter-meilisearch/src/meilisearch.ts:53-80` advertises no prefix support and only reads fuzzy.
4. **Cross-backend identity normalization is unspecified/inconsistent.** Contracts allow string/number IDs, while external adapters coerce numeric-looking strings and local memory type-tags them. Resource-to-table/index naming does not define collision-resistant canonicalization.
5. **Readiness semantics are underspecified relative to adapter health.** The docs call `/status` readiness, but the implementation neither probes a backend nor defines recovery from degraded state.
6. **Error security and diagnostic fidelity conflict.** Docs promise backend payload/credential safety, while adapter messages and server error mapping expose backend bodies/index/task detail.
7. **Swift implementation departs from exact persistence requirements.** The spec defines a bounded slug plus SHA-256 naming scheme and traversal defense; implementation uses unbounded slug plus FNV and path append behavior.
8. **Package/release acceptance is incomplete.** None of the bundles establishes a single cross-language version matrix, packed-artifact consumer test, registry provenance gate, or required CI ownership for every adapter/platform.

## Cross-cutting audits (security/determinism/limits/errors/compat)

### Findings

#### SEARCHFN-001 — Critical — Resource and document identifiers collide across tenants/backends

**Evidence: directly verified/static.** PostgreSQL resource normalization replaces non-alphanumerics with underscores before constructing a physical table name (`searchfn/adapter-postgres/src/postgres-schema.ts:25-36`, `searchfn/adapter-postgres/src/postgres-schema.ts:49-51`), so distinct values such as `foo-bar` and `foo_bar` collide unless the separate length-hash branch happens to apply. Elasticsearch uses the same collision-prone transformation (`searchfn/adapter-elasticsearch/src/elasticsearch.ts:38-40`, `searchfn/adapter-elasticsearch/src/elasticsearch.ts:116-118`). PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch coerce numeric-looking string IDs to numbers (`searchfn/adapter-postgres/src/postgres.ts:71-79`, `searchfn/adapter-elasticsearch/src/elasticsearch.ts:42-50`); IndexedDB uses `String(id)` (`searchfn/adapter-indexeddb/src/index.ts:762-790`, `searchfn/adapter-indexeddb/src/index.ts:827-837`), while memory explicitly type-tags IDs (`searchfn/adapter-memory/src/index.ts:187-189`). Thus `"1"` and `1` can alias or move identity when switching adapters.

**Impact:** two logical resources can share storage; documents can overwrite/delete/return across resource or tenant boundaries; migration between adapters changes identity.

**Required fix:** define one versioned, collision-resistant resource-key and document-ID encoding in adapter contracts; include type tags and a cryptographic hash; migrate existing physical names; add adversarial cross-adapter conformance vectors.

#### SEARCHFN-002 — High — Authorization observes a different payload than request handlers

**Evidence: static.** Auth payload parsing returns `null` for non-JSON content types (`searchfn/server/src/server.ts:210-227`), but JSON handlers parse bodies regardless of content type (`searchfn/server/src/routes/search.ts:16-63`). An authorization callback that scopes access using payload/resource can therefore approve `null` while a `text/plain` JSON body executes. User limits are blindly merged into defaults (`searchfn/server/src/server.ts:75-86`). Numeric validation permits fractional limits (`searchfn/server/src/http/validation.ts:75-101`), document fields/ID/array shapes are shallow (`searchfn/server/src/http/validation.ts:122-155`), and fuzzy distance is effectively unbounded (`searchfn/server/src/http/validation.ts:228-243`). The client validates only that documents are an array/count, not document content (`searchfn/client/src/client.ts:81-90`).

**Impact:** tenant/resource authorization can be bypassed by content-type mismatch; invalid/high-cost payloads cross the public boundary.

#### SEARCHFN-003 — High — Canonical errors disclose backend bodies and infrastructure details

**Evidence: static.** The server forwards every recognized `SearchAdapterError`, including INTERNAL, with its message (`searchfn/server/src/http/errors.ts:73-80`). Elasticsearch bulk failures include index, document ID, and backend error JSON (`searchfn/adapter-elasticsearch/src/elasticsearch.ts:62-70`, `searchfn/adapter-elasticsearch/src/elasticsearch.ts:236-245`), and the low-level client includes arbitrary response bodies (`searchfn/adapter-elasticsearch/src/elastic-client.ts:146-153`). Meilisearch does the same for HTTP/task failures (`searchfn/adapter-meilisearch/src/meili-client.ts:153-160`, `searchfn/adapter-meilisearch/src/meili-client.ts:173-195`). Documentation promises that credentials/backend payloads are not leaked (`searchfn/docs/content/docs/operations/security.mdx:34-45`).

**Impact:** public callers can learn tenant index names, document IDs, backend topology, or sensitive provider messages.

#### SEARCHFN-004 — High — `/status` is a sticky local flag, not backend readiness

**Evidence: static.** Status returns a local snapshot without probing adapter connectivity or operation health (`searchfn/server/src/routes/status.ts:11-29`). Any 5xx/exception marks the server degraded and there is no recovery path (`searchfn/server/src/server.ts:88-98`, `searchfn/server/src/server.ts:134-158`). Docs present the endpoint as readiness (`searchfn/docs/content/docs/operations/observability.mdx:47-70`).

**Impact:** an unreachable backend can report ready until a request fails; one transient error can report degraded forever after recovery. Orchestrators will route or evict incorrectly.

#### SEARCHFN-005 — High — IndexedDB search and persistence are not a consistent snapshot

**Evidence: static.** Mutations serialize through a queue (`searchfn/adapter-indexeddb/src/index.ts:529-544`, `searchfn/adapter-indexeddb/src/index.ts:743-797`), but search does not wait for that queue (`searchfn/adapter-indexeddb/src/index.ts:799-824`). `persistAll` performs five separate writes/transactions and clears dirty postings before all other writes complete (`searchfn/adapter-indexeddb/src/index.ts:646-695`). Hydration parses persisted JSON without corruption handling (`searchfn/adapter-indexeddb/src/index.ts:431-473`). The IndexedDB manager has no `onblocked`/`onversionchange` lifecycle (`searchfn/core/src/storage/indexeddb-manager.ts:66-108`, `searchfn/core/src/storage/indexeddb-manager.ts:126-143`). A default logger can emit database names without explicit observability opt-in (`searchfn/core/src/utils/logger.ts:3-20`, `searchfn/core/src/storage/indexeddb-manager.ts:72-77`).

**Impact:** reads can see half-applied state, crashes can persist inconsistent generations, corruption can brick initialization, and upgrades can hang.

#### SEARCHFN-006 — High — Swift SQLite persistence violates naming, containment, atomicity, and lifecycle requirements

**Evidence: static.** The spec requires a bounded slug plus first 16 SHA-256 characters and traversal rejection (`searchfn/.conduct/specs/2026-03-28-new-s7k4m2p9-spec/SPEC.md:242-263`, `searchfn/.conduct/specs/2026-03-28-new-s7k4m2p9-spec/SPEC.md:350-364`). Code uses an unbounded slug plus FNV-1a 64 (`searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter/SearchFnSQLiteStore.swift:22-55`). Only the convenience initializer checks non-empty/file URLs (`searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnConvenience/SearchFn.swift:9-17`); direct configuration does not. Directory creation/path append lacks canonical/symlink containment (`searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter/SearchFnSQLiteStore.swift:14-20`, `searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter/SearchFnSQLiteStore.swift:94-113`). Batch indexing writes documents one-by-one, then updates memory only after the full loop (`searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter.swift:86-100`), so failure/cancellation splits disk and cache. Declared cache limits are unused (`searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter.swift:5-29`). Initialization hydrates all documents (`searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter.swift:265-281`; select-all at `searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter/SearchFnSQLiteStore.swift:150-171`), while posting tables are not the search source. Schema migration and manifest update are not one transaction (`searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter/SearchFnSQLiteStore.swift:305-367`). Initialization deletes persisted resources omitted from the current list (`searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter.swift:67-83`), and disposed adapters cannot be reinitialized (`searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter/SearchFnSQLiteAdapter.swift:241-244`; memory equivalent at `searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnMemoryAdapter/SearchFnMemoryAdapter.swift:34-36`, `searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnMemoryAdapter/SearchFnMemoryAdapter.swift:207-210`).

**Impact:** path escape through pre-existing symlinks, data deletion, cache/disk divergence, unbounded memory, and unusable lifecycle recovery.

#### SEARCHFN-007 — High — Python package is an alpha prototype without bounded or transactional indexing

**Evidence: directly verified/static.** Metadata labels the distribution alpha and contains an assumed dependency (`searchfn/python/pyproject.toml:5-25`). No migration creates the required `_searchfn_index`. The server drops request context/authorization and directly exposes reindex/search (`searchfn/python/src/searchfn/server.py:20-72`). Reindex loads all source records, deletes/reinserts row-by-row without a transaction, and does not purge deleted source records (`searchfn/python/src/searchfn/indexing.py:58-121`). The delete loop can fail to progress when malformed rows are not removed (`searchfn/python/src/searchfn/indexing.py:15-55`), and duplicate detection heuristically parses strings (`searchfn/python/src/searchfn/indexing.py:6-12`). Search executes an unbounded database query per token with no query/token/candidate cap (`searchfn/python/src/searchfn/search.py:16-62`). Only two tests cover basic behavior (`searchfn/python/tests/test_search.py:39-74`), and the README calls it prototype/MVP-scale (`searchfn/python/README.md:128-137`).

**Impact:** denial of service, stale/partial indexes, authorization bypass, and non-deployable schema assumptions.

#### SEARCHFN-008 — High — Published package graph/build surfaces are inconsistent

**Evidence: static.** Client declares subpath exports that its single-entry tsup build does not create (`searchfn/client/package.json:10-25`, `searchfn/client/tsup.config.ts:3-13`). The DataFn provider publishes a `file:` dependency on adapter contracts (`searchfn/datafn-provider/package.json:50-55`). PostgreSQL docs import nonexistent `getPostgresMigrationSQL` (`searchfn/docs/content/docs/reference/adapters/postgres.mdx:20-29`); its package index does not export that API (`searchfn/adapter-postgres/src/index.ts:1-20`). core-wasm declares CJS but its loader uses `import.meta` (`searchfn/core-wasm/package.json:10-15`, `searchfn/core-wasm/src/index.ts:165-180`). Rust tests define duplicate test function names, which statically guarantees a Cargo E0428 compile failure (`searchfn/core-wasm/rust/src/lib.rs:494-546`), while the npm test script does not run `cargo test` (`searchfn/core-wasm/package.json:20-28`). Package versions are split across 0.1.0/0.3.0 and several packages omit a Node engine/publish policy.

**Impact:** packed packages can contain broken exports/dependencies, documented imports fail, and Rust tests are never a valid release signal.

#### SEARCHFN-009 — Medium — Meilisearch prefix/default/error behavior contradicts its spec

**Evidence: static.** Capabilities report `prefix: false` (`searchfn/adapter-meilisearch/src/meilisearch.ts:53-61`) despite p7 ADP-011 requiring native prefix support. Defaults store several options but only fuzzy is used (`searchfn/adapter-meilisearch/src/meilisearch.ts:65-80`, `searchfn/adapter-meilisearch/src/meilisearch.ts:143-159`, `searchfn/adapter-meilisearch/src/meilisearch.ts:169-194`), so prefix/field boosts are ignored and ADP-012 fails. Successful malformed JSON can be accepted as a string (`searchfn/adapter-meilisearch/src/meili-client.ts:90-99`, `searchfn/adapter-meilisearch/src/meili-client.ts:223-229`), allowing empty/silent success paths. Task polling is a fixed 50 ms loop for up to roughly two minutes and bodies are read whole (`searchfn/adapter-meilisearch/src/meili-client.ts:173-195`).

#### SEARCHFN-010 — Medium — External adapters lack safe configuration and response/batch bounds

**Evidence: static.** PostgreSQL `maxBatchSize` is not validated; zero/negative values can make chunk iteration non-progressing (`searchfn/adapter-postgres/src/postgres.ts:100-103`, `searchfn/adapter-postgres/src/postgres.ts:172-180`). Empty fields can produce an invalid empty insert (`searchfn/adapter-postgres/src/postgres.ts:186-219`), and AbortSignal checks are not attached to in-flight database queries. Elasticsearch sends a whole batch as one bulk payload (`searchfn/adapter-elasticsearch/src/elasticsearch.ts:222-245`), ignores every HTTP 400 during index creation (`searchfn/adapter-elasticsearch/src/elasticsearch.ts:183-207`), and defaults to zero replicas (`searchfn/adapter-elasticsearch/src/elasticsearch.ts:193-199`). Elasticsearch/Meili read response bodies whole (`searchfn/adapter-elasticsearch/src/elastic-client.ts:193-210`, `searchfn/adapter-meilisearch/src/meili-client.ts:214-229`). Retry counts are lower-bounded but not upper-bounded in the duplicated adapter retry helpers (for example `searchfn/adapter-postgres/src/internal/retry.ts:31-52`).

**Positive boundary:** PostgreSQL parameterizes values, quotes identifiers, and uses per-batch transactions; Elasticsearch/Meili have request timeouts, merged abort signals, retry helpers, and redaction hooks.

#### SEARCHFN-011 — Medium — Native/fallback/provider paths do not share deterministic completeness semantics

**Evidence: static.** Server `searchAll` trusts adapter-native ordering/limit while only the fallback performs canonical sorting (`searchfn/server/src/routes/search-all.ts:98-110`). The DataFn provider maps native results without sorting/capping (`searchfn/datafn-provider/src/index.ts:104-121`), while its fallback silently returns partial results when some resources fail (`searchfn/datafn-provider/src/index.ts:136-181`). `updateIndices` can turn a missing resource value into the literal `"undefined"` (`searchfn/datafn-provider/src/index.ts:88-101`). Legacy `InMemorySearchFn` lacks the newer query/fuzzy-distance caps (`searchfn/client/src/in-memory-search.ts:139-180`, `searchfn/client/src/in-memory-search.ts:322-340`).

**Evidence: directly verified/static.** The SearchFn workflow is path-filtered to and tests only the client (`.github/workflows/searchfn-client-tests.yml:1-41`); the Tusk workflow likewise centers on client coverage. ### Security, validation, and tenant boundaries

- **Blocking:** collision-prone resource/index/table names and cross-adapter ID coercion violate tenant/resource isolation.
- Authorization must receive the exact validated canonical body later executed by a route. Content type, parse, validation, and auth should be a single pipeline with immutable output.
- Public errors must map INTERNAL/backend errors to stable safe messages and private correlation IDs; provider bodies/index/task details belong only in redacted opt-in diagnostics.
- Swift paths must be canonicalized beneath an owned root, reject symlink escapes, and use the specified collision-resistant name.
- Python server routes need context propagation and explicit authorization before any search/reindex access.

### Determinism, limits, and errors

- Strong positive ordering exists in the main client (`searchfn/client/src/client.ts:61-69`, `searchfn/client/src/client.ts:155-190`), memory (`searchfn/adapter-memory/src/index.ts:458-466`), IndexedDB (`searchfn/adapter-indexeddb/src/index.ts:903-911`), PostgreSQL (`searchfn/adapter-postgres/src/postgres.ts:315-324`), Elasticsearch (`searchfn/adapter-elasticsearch/src/elasticsearch.ts:320-325`), and Swift client (`searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnClient/SearchFnClient.swift:326-335`).
- Native `searchAll`, provider fallback, document identity, and some legacy APIs do not share those invariants.
- Request streaming caps are a strong boundary (`searchfn/server/src/http/errors.ts:86-157`), but document/value depth, fuzzy distance, response bodies, batches, retry count, Python queries, and Swift hydration are not adequately bounded.
- Canonical error codes/types exist, but message exposure and cross-runtime mapping are inconsistent.

### Compatibility and migrations

- Package-per-adapter dependencies mostly isolate browser client code from PostgreSQL/external SDKs, a strong architectural invariant.
- The same revision contains “no compatibility,” mandatory compatibility, destructive aggregate removal, and wrapper-retention policies. Release work cannot be safely judged until one precedence decision resolves them.
- The failed canonical-source guard proves the aggregate cleanup is incomplete.
- Cross-adapter migrations need explicit resource-name and typed-document-ID encoding before any production data is moved.
- Swift schema/manifest, IndexedDB schema changes, Python index creation, and versioned package migrations lack production-grade rollout/rollback proof.

### Operational, release, and packaging readiness

- `/status` cannot act as a reliable readiness gate.
- No full adapter/server/provider/platform CI or mandatory integration/load/performance matrix exists.
- Package exports, `file:` dependency, documented nonexistent API, CJS/import-meta mismatch, duplicate Rust tests, and split versions block coordinated publication.
- External clients have useful timeout/retry/redaction primitives, but batching, body caps, backend health, failure recovery, and diagnostic safety require hardening.
- Docs are broad and well-structured, but several operational/security statements are stronger than implementation.

- Adapter contracts define canonical error codes and capability declarations.
- Main client and canonical adapters deliberately sort deterministically.
- Memory adapter type-tags IDs internally, isolates resources, and supports reinitialization.

## Recommendations (ranked)

Fix in this order:

1. **Protect isolation:** version a collision-resistant resource key and typed document-ID encoding; patch PostgreSQL/Elastic/IDB behavior; ship explicit data migrations and cross-adapter conformance tests.
2. **Unify the request trust pipeline:** require JSON for JSON routes, parse once, deeply validate bounded documents/options, authorize the canonical parsed body, and pass that same object to handlers.
3. **Make errors safe and health truthful:** sanitize all public INTERNAL/backend messages, preserve private correlation diagnostics, add real adapter health probes and recoverable readiness state.
4. **Repair persistence:** make IndexedDB generations atomically committable/read-consistent with corruption/upgrade handling; implement Swift path containment, specified hashing, atomic batch/cache semantics, bounded hydration, safe lifecycle and migrations.
5. **Decide canonical compatibility policy:** publish one precedence decision, remove or convert every aggregate file accordingly, restore/export-baseline guards, finish DataFn MiniSearch migration, and make the canonical guard pass in root CI.
6. **Harden adapters/Python:** validate batch/retry/timeout/value limits; stream/cap responses; attach cancellation to real queries; fix Meili capabilities/defaults; redesign Python schema/auth/index transactions and caps.
7. **Fix package artifacts:** create every declared client subpath, replace `file:` dependencies, export or remove documented APIs, correct WASM module formats/tests, align engines/versions/publish metadata, and consumer-test packed artifacts.
8. **Build a release matrix:** require core/contracts/client/server/provider/all adapters, canonical guard, Docker integrations, Rust, Swift, Python, docs, browser/WASM, security, and benchmark thresholds in CI.
9. **Correct docs/local guidance:** replace the dangling `AGENTS.md` link with a tracked portable file; reconcile readiness/security/prefix/PostgreSQL docs with verified behavior.

Production gate: do not release the multi-backend SearchFn surface until SEARCHFN-001 through SEARCHFN-008 and SEARCHFN-013 are closed, all 19 FAIL occurrences are resolved or explicitly superseded, the bundle precedence decision is recorded, the canonical guard passes, packed artifacts install in consumers, and supported live adapters/platforms pass the release matrix.

| Python | `searchfn` 0.1.0 alpha | Prototype only; no production schema/auth/bounds. |
| Swift | `SearchFnSwift` | Architecture present; SQLite security/atomicity/lifecycle blocker. |

### Evidence boundaries

- Paths are repository-relative and portable; the machine-specific dangling-symlink target is deliberately not reproduced.
- Line evidence applies only to the pinned commit.
- PASS denotes static source coverage unless a runtime result explicitly says otherwise.
- Existing SearchFn audits and phase reports were historical inputs only and did not establish compliance.
- External DataFn, backend, browser, registry, CI, Rust, Swift, and Python behavior remains unverified unless stated.

arguments.content:
# ApiFn production-readiness audit

## Metadata

- Audit date: 2026-08-11
- Auditor: `audit_api_search`
- Model: GPT-5 (Codex)
- Launcher: Codex Desktop
- Repository state: detached `HEAD` at `721eefdd9cd716894e5329123a9e2fb615783611`
- Scope root: `apifn/`
- Method: independent, read-only source and specification review. Existing audit conclusions were not used as compliance evidence.
- Evidence labels:
  - **Directly verified**: observed in the pinned tree or produced by a read-only command in this audit.
  - **Static**: conclusion from source/configuration inspection; the relevant runtime was not executed.
  - **Unverified**: requires a build, package, browser, external service, registry, or CI environment that was not exercised.
- Overall decision: **NO-GO for production**. One critical exploit path and six high-severity correctness, security, interoperability, and release blockers remain.

## Audit scope

This audit covers the complete ApiFn product surface present at the pinned commit:

- TypeScript packages: `apifn/core`, `apifn/collections`, `apifn/cli`, `apifn/mock`, `apifn/snippets`, `apifn/docsfn`, `apifn/react`, and `apifn/svelte`.
- Python distribution: `apifn/python`, including FastAPI and Flask adapters.
- Cross-function integrations: authfn, secfn, logfn, watchfn, testfn, and docsfn integration code owned by ApiFn.
- Public documentation, examples, CI example/workflow, package manifests, exports, build/test scripts, release metadata, fixtures, and tests.
- ApiFn intent plus the complete specification bundle, including all principal documents, 26 phase files, and 26 phase reports. Phase reports and prior audits were treated as historical claims only; implementation was checked independently.

The static inventory contains **251 regular files** under `apifn/` after excluding generated/dependency directories. The largest areas are `.conduct` (62), collections (42), core (36), CLI (32), snippets (20), Python (13), React (13), Svelte (11), docsfn (10), mock (9), examples (1), and the root README (1). Fifty test-related/fixture files and approximately 292 `it`/`test` declarations were found by static search; neither count is a claim that those tests execute or pass.

## Inputs audited (intent + spec bundles)

### Authoritative intent and product documentation

- `apifn/.conduct/intent-v0.md`
- `apifn/README.md`
- Package READMEs, inline API documentation, `apifn/examples/`, and `apifn/examples/ci-cd/github-actions.yml`

### Specification bundle

Bundle: `apifn/.conduct/specs/2026-03-05-new-k4m7x9r2-spec/`

- Principal documents: `INTENT_AUDIT.md`, `SPEC.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `TEST_VECTORS.md`, `PLAN.md`, and `logs.csv`.
- Plans: `phases/PHASE_00.md` through `phases/PHASE_25.md` (26/26 inventoried and inspected).
- Completion claims: `phase-reports/PHASE_00_REPORT.md` through `phase-reports/PHASE_25_REPORT.md` (26/26 inventoried and inspected as non-authoritative history).
- Parsed requirement inventory: **141 unique requirement IDs**. This conflicts with the bundle's statement that there are 103 requirements.

### Runtime, packaging, and verification inputs

- All `src/` trees, adapters/integrations, tests, fixtures, examples, `package.json`, `tsup.config.ts`, TypeScript/Vitest configurations, Python `pyproject.toml`, and workflow YAML under `apifn/`.
- Commands used: pinned-commit/status checks; `find`, `rg`, and `jq` inventories; requirement-ID parsing and manifest/export/script inspection.
- Not run: package installation, build, lint, unit/integration tests, browser tests, Python tests, package packing/publishing, live mock/serve processes, external integrations, or CI. The audit was constrained to read-only work and did not install dependencies or create build/test artifacts.

## High-level findings

| Severity | Count | Headline |
|---|---:|---|
| Critical | 1 | `apifn serve` inserts specification-controlled text into `innerHTML`, exposes the service on all interfaces, and enables wildcard CORS. |
| High | 6 | Resource caps are mostly declarative; authfn and OpenAPI contracts diverge; docs generation and mocking are materially incomplete; the documented CI path is not runnable as published. |
| Medium | 6 | Collection fidelity, runner semantics, UI adapters, Python parity, package exports, and observability remain incomplete or unsafe. |
| Low | 1 | Requirement accounting undercounts the normative requirement set by 38 IDs. |

Coverage verdict across the 141 normative IDs: **77 PASS, 48 PARTIAL, 15 FAIL, 1 UNVERIFIED**. A PASS below means the requirement is supported by direct/static source evidence, not that runtime acceptance tests passed.

## Intent Inventory

The bundle identifies 35 intent items. The following inventory preserves the bundle's mapping while recording implementation outcome at the feature level.

| # | Intent | Requirement coverage | Implementation outcome |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Generate OpenAPI 3.1 from HTTP routes | INTRO, OPENAPI | Partial: generation exists; deduplication, collision handling, caps, and full 3.0 conversion do not. |
| 2 | Zod/TypeBox schema validation | SCHEMA | Partial: integrations exist; the declared draft and validation API diverge. |
| 3 | Git-native OpenCollection YAML | COLL | Partial: reader/writer exists, but validation is shallow and fidelity/interoperability is unproven. |
| 4 | Breaking-change detection | DIFF | Partial: deterministic diff exists; caps and several compatibility semantics are incomplete. |
| 5 | Environment sets | ENV | Partial: core resolution exists; ordinary process-environment precedence and caps are incomplete. |
| 6 | React and Svelte API explorer | UI-R, UI-S | Partial: React is usable statically; Svelte has compile/type defects and both lack real tests. |
| 7 | Try-it plus live performance overlay | UI-R/UI-S, WATCH | Partial: UI and watch integration exist but are unsafe/incomplete. |
| 8 | Request history and response diff | UI-R/UI-S | Partial: local components exist; specified persistence/caps and verification are incomplete. |
| 9 | `apifn serve` | CLI, SERVE | Fail: unsafe static HTML shell, no complete explorer/router/proxy behavior. |
| 10 | `apifn test` and collection runner | CLI, RUN, ASSERT | Partial: runner is substantial; cancellation, retries, limits, and reporting isolation diverge. |
| 11 | `apifn diff` | CLI, CI | Partial: command exists; CI/release path is broken. |
| 12 | `apifn export` | CLI | Partial: command exists; normalization/size and interoperability remain incomplete/unverified. |
| 13 | docsfn API reference component | DOCS | Fail: the package does not export/build the required renderer surface. |
| 14 | Embedded docs try-it | DOCS | Fail: no complete embedded runtime integration. |
| 15 | docsfn auto-sidebar | DOCS | Partial: generated pages exist but tag/slug semantics are lossy. |
| 16 | FastAPI/Flask introspection | PY | Partial: adapters exist but are shallow and lack TypeScript parity. |
| 17 | Self-hosted | Architectural | Present, but exposed defaults are unsafe for production. |
| 18 | Git-native collections | COLL | Partial for the same fidelity/interoperability reasons as item 3. |
| 19 | Schema-from-code with no separate YAML | INTRO, OPENAPI | Partial: route introspection exists, but schema semantics are incomplete. |
| 20 | Endpoint performance data | WATCH | Partial: metrics types/integration exist; robust runtime behavior is not established. |
| 21 | Embedded docs site | DOCS | Fail at the required public/package surface. |
| 22 | Breaking-change CI | DIFF, CLI, CI | Fail as a consumable workflow despite working diff primitives. |
| 23 | authfn short-lived test tokens | AUTH | Partial: integration exists but violates the specified request/expiry/override contract. |
| 24 | secfn and logfn integration | SEC, LOG | Partial: redaction exists; CLI logging and URL leakage remain. |
| 25 | p50/p95/p99, error rate, volume via watchfn | WATCH | Partial: types and display paths exist; external contract was not verified. |
| 26 | Postman/Bruno-like API documentation and testing | RUN, ASSERT | Partial: meaningful runner functionality exists, not production parity. |
| 27 | Automatic docs generation | DOCS | Fail at package integration/rendering surface. |
| 28 | Deployed API monitoring via watchfn | WATCH | Partial and externally unverified. |
| 29 | OpenCollection/Bruno interoperability | COLL | Unverified externally; local format handling is only partial. |
| 30 | Comparable core capabilities to Postman/Bruno/Swagger/Scalar | Positioning | Not achieved at production quality. |
| 31 | Mock server | MOCK | Partial: server works statically but validation, generation, CORS, and binding are unsafe. |
| 32 | Code snippets | SNIP | Pass statically across all seven requirements. |
| 33 | GitHub Actions integration | CI | Fail as located/documented. |
| 34 | testfn adapter | TESTFN | Pass statically; live package compatibility remains unverified. |
| 35 | Multi-framework UI | UI-R, UI-S | Partial; Svelte is not release-ready. |

## Intent → Spec coverage matrix

| Intent(s) | SPEC area | Requirement IDs | Bundle test vectors/phases |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1, 19 | Core generation, introspection rules | INTRO-001–005; OPENAPI-001–010 | TV-INTRO/OPENAPI; phases 02, 04 |
| 2 | Schema descriptors and validation | SCHEMA-001–005 | TV-SCHEMA; phase 03 |
| 3, 18, 29 | OpenCollection YAML and Bruno interop | COLL-001–007 | TV-COLL; phases 06–07 |
| 4, 11, 22 | OpenAPI diff, CLI, and CI | DIFF-001–009; CLI-005; CI-001–004 | TV-DIFF/CLI/CI; phases 13–14, 25 |
| 5 | Environment semantics | ENV-001–005 | TV-ENV; phase 08 |
| 6, 35 | React/Svelte explorers | UI-R-001–009; UI-S-001–009 | TV-UI; phases 18–19 |
| 7 | Try-it and performance overlay | UI-R-004/007; UI-S-004/007 | Corresponding TV-UI; phases 18–19, 21 |
| 8 | Request history and response diff | UI-R-005–006; UI-S-005–006 | Corresponding TV-UI; phases 18–19 |
| 9 | Local explorer server | CLI-006; SERVE-001–004 | TV-CLI/SERVE; phase 17 |
| 10, 26 | Collection execution/assertions | CLI-004; RUN-001–011; ASSERT-001–007 | TV-RUN/ASSERT; phases 10–12 |
| 12 | OpenAPI export | CLI-003 | TV-CLI-003; phase 09 |
| 13–15, 21, 27 | docsfn reference, try-it, navigation | DOCS-001–006 | TV-DOCS; phase 20 |
| 16 | Python SDK/adapters | PY-001–005 | TV-PY; phase 24 |
| 17, 30 | Self-hosting and product positioning | Architectural goals/non-goals | Whole plan; no discrete acceptance ID |
| 20, 25, 28 | watchfn integration | WATCH-001–004 | TV-WATCH; phase 21 |
| 23 | authfn token minting | AUTH-001–003 | TV-AUTH; phase 22 |
| 24 | secfn/logfn | SEC-001–002; LOG-001–002 | TV-SEC/LOG; phase 22 |
| 31 | Mock server | MOCK-001–007 | TV-MOCK; phases 16–17 |
| 32 | Snippet generation | SNIP-001–007 | TV-SNIP; phase 15 |
| 33 | GitHub Actions | CI-001–004 | TV-CI; phase 25 |
| 34 | testfn adapter | TESTFN-001–003 | TV-TESTFN; phase 23 |

The matrix has no unmapped intent item. The gap is implementation and verification, not missing spec traceability. The architectural intents (17 and 30) lack independently testable acceptance IDs.

## Requirement coverage summary

| Category | Total | PASS | PARTIAL | FAIL | UNVERIFIED |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| CORE | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| INTRO | 5 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| SCHEMA | 5 | 3 | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| OPENAPI | 13 | 10 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| COLL | 7 | 2 | 3 | 1 | 1 |
| ENV | 5 | 3 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| CLI | 11 | 6 | 4 | 1 | 0 |
| RUN | 11 | 5 | 6 | 0 | 0 |
| ASSERT | 7 | 6 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| DIFF | 9 | 6 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| UI-R | 9 | 6 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| UI-S | 9 | 0 | 8 | 1 | 0 |
| SERVE | 4 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| DOCS | 6 | 0 | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| SNIP | 7 | 7 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| MOCK | 7 | 3 | 3 | 1 | 0 |
| WATCH | 4 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| AUTH | 3 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 0 |

| LOG | 2 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| TESTFN | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| PY | 5 | 1 | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| CI | 4 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| **Total** | **141** | **77** | **48** | **15** | **1** |

## Requirement-by-requirement results

Every parsed normative requirement ID appears below exactly once. Grouping keeps the matrix reviewable; the source findings following it explain the material PARTIAL/FAIL decisions.

| Category | PASS | PARTIAL | FAIL | UNVERIFIED |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CORE | CORE-001, CORE-002, CORE-003 | — | — | — |
| INTRO | INTRO-001, INTRO-002, INTRO-003, INTRO-004, INTRO-005 | — | — | — |
| SCHEMA | SCHEMA-002, SCHEMA-003, SCHEMA-004 | — | SCHEMA-001, SCHEMA-005 | — |
| OPENAPI | OPENAPI-002, OPENAPI-003, OPENAPI-004, OPENAPI-005, OPENAPI-006, OPENAPI-007, OPENAPI-008, OPENAPI-009, OPENAPI-010, OPENAPI-011 | OPENAPI-001, OPENAPI-012, OPENAPI-013 | — | — |
| COLL | COLL-004, COLL-005 | COLL-001, COLL-002, COLL-007 | COLL-003 | COLL-006 |
| ENV | ENV-002, ENV-003, ENV-005 | ENV-001 | ENV-004 | — |
| CLI | CLI-001, CLI-002, CLI-003, CLI-005, CLI-008, CLI-009 | CLI-004, CLI-007, CLI-010, CLI-011 | CLI-006 | — |
| RUN | RUN-001, RUN-004, RUN-005, RUN-009, RUN-010 | RUN-002, RUN-003, RUN-006, RUN-007, RUN-008, RUN-011 | — | — |
| ASSERT | ASSERT-001, ASSERT-002, ASSERT-003, ASSERT-004, ASSERT-005, ASSERT-007 | ASSERT-006 | — | — |
| DIFF | DIFF-001, DIFF-002, DIFF-006, DIFF-007, DIFF-008, DIFF-009 | DIFF-003, DIFF-004, DIFF-005 | — | — |
| UI-R | UI-R-001, UI-R-002, UI-R-003, UI-R-005, UI-R-006, UI-R-007 | UI-R-004, UI-R-008, UI-R-009 | — | — |
| UI-S | — | UI-S-002, UI-S-003, UI-S-004, UI-S-005, UI-S-006, UI-S-007, UI-S-008, UI-S-009 | UI-S-001 | — |
| SERVE | SERVE-002 | SERVE-001 | SERVE-003, SERVE-004 | — |
| DOCS | — | DOCS-001, DOCS-004, DOCS-006 | DOCS-002, DOCS-003, DOCS-005 | — |
| SNIP | SNIP-001, SNIP-002, SNIP-003, SNIP-004, SNIP-005, SNIP-006, SNIP-007 | — | — | — |
| MOCK | MOCK-001, MOCK-003, MOCK-006 | MOCK-002, MOCK-004, MOCK-005 | MOCK-007 | — |
| WATCH | WATCH-001, WATCH-002 | WATCH-004 | WATCH-003 | — |
| AUTH | AUTH-003 | AUTH-001, AUTH-002 | — | — |
| SEC | SEC-001, SEC-002 | — | — | — |
| LOG | — | LOG-001 | LOG-002 | — |
| TESTFN | TESTFN-001, TESTFN-002, TESTFN-003 | — | — | — |
| PY | PY-001 | PY-002, PY-003, PY-004, PY-005 | — | — |
| CI | CI-002, CI-003 | CI-004 | CI-001 | — |

`COLL-006` is UNVERIFIED because its core acceptance claim is real Bruno/OpenCollection interoperability; local parsing and fixtures cannot prove behavior against Bruno 3+.

## Spec conflicts / spec gaps

1. **Requirement count is internally inconsistent.** `INTENT_AUDIT.md:108-116` claims 103 individual requirements, while parsing `REQUIREMENTS.md` yields 141 unique IDs. Nine UI-S IDs are also encoded as a list beneath one heading, making heading-only accounting undercount further.
2. **The schema draft target conflicts with implementation.** The spec requires JSON Schema 2020-12; Zod conversion declares 2019-09 (`apifn/core/src/schema/zod.ts:26-32`).
3. **Declared limits are not attached to enforceable boundaries.** The bundle specifies limits including 10,000 routes, depth 20, 50 MB OpenAPI input, 5,000 collection items, concurrency 50, 300,000 ms timeout, TTL 3,600 s, 1,000 environment variables, 10 s scripts, 10 MB capture, history 500, and 10,000 diff changes. Most have no corresponding validator at the actual allocation/loop/read boundary.
4. **Version/release goal and package state conflict.** The bundle targets 1.0.0/Q4 2026 with no deferrals; manifests remain at 0.0.1–0.0.3 and important exports/tests/workflow surfaces are incomplete.
5. **Compatibility claims outrun proof.** OpenAPI 3.0 import/3.1 generation, OpenCollection latest, Bruno 3+, Node 18+, and Python 3.10 are specified, but no audited CI matrix or external compatibility evidence proves them.
6. **Architectural positioning is not acceptance-testable.** “Self-hosted” and competitor-comparability intents have no bounded acceptance criteria, allowing nominal compliance despite unsafe network defaults and missing product surfaces.

## Cross-cutting audits (security/determinism/limits/errors/compat)

### Findings

#### APIFN-001 — Critical — Stored XSS and unintended network exposure in `apifn serve`

**Evidence: directly verified/static.** Specification-controlled paths/summaries are interpolated into markup and assigned through `innerHTML` without escaping (`apifn/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:85-96`). The Node server listens with `listen(port)`—all interfaces—while advertising only localhost (`apifn/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:163-195`, `apifn/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:209-213`), and returns `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (`apifn/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:172`). The CLI exposes no matching `--cors` policy control (`apifn/cli/src/index.ts:296-317`). Load errors are replaced by placeholder state (`apifn/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:141-145`). The served page is a basic spec-rendered shell and does not implement the specified router, complete Try-It experience, or proxy behavior.

**Impact:** Opening a malicious or compromised OpenAPI file can execute script in the explorer origin. Network peers may reach a service users believe is localhost-only, and wildcard CORS broadens access.

**Required fix:** escape/render text with DOM-safe APIs, default-bind to loopback, require explicit host/CORS opt-in, fail closed on invalid specs, add a CSP, and test malicious spec fields plus remote-interface access.

#### APIFN-002 — High — Normative caps are largely declarative and permit resource exhaustion

**Evidence: directly verified/static.** Route introspection has no 10,000-route cap (`apifn/core/src/introspect.ts:256-270`). OpenAPI parsing reads without the 50 MB boundary (`apifn/core/src/openapi/parse.ts:9-24`, `apifn/core/src/openapi/parse.ts:48-55`). Recursive canonical sorting has no depth guard (`apifn/core/src/openapi/generate.ts:252-267`). Collection reads/validation do not enforce item/environment limits (`apifn/collections/src/reader.ts:104-175`, `apifn/collections/src/validator.ts:4-84`). Runner concurrency and timeout values are accepted without the specified maximum/finite/positive validation (`apifn/collections/src/runner/runner.ts:516-517`, `apifn/collections/src/runner/runner.ts:525-566`, `apifn/collections/src/runner/runner.ts:587`; CLI coercion at `apifn/cli/src/index.ts:239-244`). The HTTP client calls `response.text()` before capture truncation (`apifn/collections/src/runner/http-client.ts:363-370`); truncation occurs only afterward (`apifn/collections/src/runner/runner.ts:214-231`, `apifn/collections/src/runner/runner.ts:382-386`). Diff size is not bounded.

**Impact:** hostile or accidental inputs can drive excessive memory, CPU, recursion, sockets, timers, or output volume.

#### APIFN-003 — High — authfn integration violates token, expiry, timeout, and override semantics

**Evidence: static.** The request options require TTL yet omit the specified key identifier and use a string expiry shape (`apifn/core/src/integrations/authfn.ts:21-30`). TTL is only upper-bounded; no default or positive/finite validation exists (`apifn/core/src/integrations/authfn.ts:36-42`). Token minting has no request timeout (`apifn/core/src/integrations/authfn.ts:53-61`) and embeds arbitrary upstream response text in errors (`apifn/core/src/integrations/authfn.ts:63-66`). Injected auth does not reliably override collection-level authorization (`apifn/core/src/integrations/authfn.ts:76-92`).

**Impact:** collection credentials may win over intended short-lived tokens; calls can hang; upstream secrets/details can leak into logs or UI.

#### APIFN-004 — High — OpenAPI/schema output is not the specified canonical contract

**Evidence: static.** Zod conversion emits JSON Schema 2019-09 rather than 2020-12 (`apifn/core/src/schema/zod.ts:26-32`). A deduplication helper exists (`apifn/core/src/schema/dedup.ts:49-86`) but the generator imports only schema conversion and does not populate canonical `components.schemas` (`apifn/core/src/openapi/generate.ts:1`, `apifn/core/src/openapi/generate.ts:206-235`). Parser validation is mostly version checks and 3.0 nullable conversion is incomplete (`apifn/core/src/openapi/parse.ts:27-55`, `apifn/core/src/openapi/upconvert.ts:7-49`). Validation is asynchronous despite the specified surface (`apifn/core/src/openapi/validate.ts:28-36`). Duplicate method/path entries overwrite one another (`apifn/core/src/openapi/generate.ts:206-235`).

**Impact:** generated documents can silently lose routes, drift from the declared draft, or fail downstream tooling.

#### APIFN-005 — High — docsfn package cannot deliver the specified reference/try-it integration

**Evidence: static.** The package exports/builds only its root (`apifn/docsfn/package.json:9-15`, `apifn/docsfn/package.json:53-55`; `apifn/docsfn/tsup.config.ts:3-9`), while the root exports do not expose the required renderer/component surface (`apifn/docsfn/src/index.ts:8-23`). Options accept only `spec`/`specPath` rather than the specified Router/watchfn integration (`apifn/docsfn/src/types.ts:66-82`, `apifn/docsfn/src/provider.ts:161-185`). Page grouping uses only the first tag and slug construction can collide (`apifn/docsfn/src/provider.ts:28-46`, `apifn/docsfn/src/provider.ts:136-149`).

**Impact:** consumers cannot import the promised UI/reference integration from the published package; generated navigation can lose or overwrite endpoints.

#### APIFN-006 — High — Mock server trust boundaries and generated responses are unsafe/inaccurate

**Evidence: static.** The server binds all interfaces by default (`apifn/mock/src/server.ts:257-266`). CORS joins multiple origins into one invalid header and permits dangerous wildcard/credential combinations while ignoring requested methods/headers (`apifn/mock/src/server.ts:75-91`); OPTIONS succeeds for arbitrary paths (`apifn/mock/src/server.ts:191-196`). Request validation supports only a small schema subset and skips `$ref` (`apifn/mock/src/request-validator.ts:20-24`, `apifn/mock/src/request-validator.ts:118-121`, `apifn/mock/src/request-validator.ts:158-160`). Response generation ignores important constraints and can emit schema-invalid values (`apifn/mock/src/response-generator.ts:17-55`, `apifn/mock/src/response-generator.ts:72-111`).

**Impact:** a “validating” mock can accept invalid calls and return invalid examples, undermining tests while exposing an unnecessary network listener.

#### APIFN-007 — High — The advertised CI workflow is not consumable or internally consistent

**Evidence: directly verified/static.** The reusable workflow is stored under `apifn/.github/workflows/api-check.yml`, not the repository root workflow directory. The example calls a repository-local workflow path that GitHub cannot resolve as a reusable workflow (`apifn/examples/ci-cd/github-actions.yml:9-17`). The workflow builds `@apifn/cli` but invokes `npx --yes apifn` (`apifn/.github/workflows/api-check.yml:85-89`, `apifn/.github/workflows/api-check.yml:107-151`); the package is named `@apifn/cli` with bin `apifn` (`apifn/cli/package.json:2-10`). The README advertises this path (`apifn/README.md:5-16`, `apifn/README.md:27-29`).

**Impact:** the primary breaking-change gate can fail before checking an API or can fetch a different/unavailable registry package.

#### APIFN-008 — Medium — Collection/environment handling is lossy and misclassifies failures

**Evidence: static.** Validation is a shallow hand-written check, not the OpenCollection schema (`apifn/collections/src/validator.ts:4-84`). The reader maps broad exceptions to “not found” and casts environment shapes without validating them (`apifn/collections/src/reader.ts:104-112`, `apifn/collections/src/reader.ts:133-139`). The writer reconstructs known fields, dropping extensions/unknown data (`apifn/collections/src/writer.ts:65-91`). Variable precedence omits the ordinary process-environment fallback described by the spec (`apifn/collections/src/variables.ts:25-87`).

**Positive boundary:** output path traversal is explicitly rejected (`apifn/collections/src/writer.ts:6-31`).

#### APIFN-009 — Medium — Runner cancellation, retry, reporting, and logging semantics are inconsistent

**Evidence: static.** The Promise timeout does not necessarily abort a custom HTTP client (`apifn/collections/src/runner/runner.ts:192-211`, `apifn/collections/src/runner/runner.ts:304-316`). Retries cover thrown errors and 5xx responses, not the full specified failure policy such as assertion failures/eligible 4xx (`apifn/collections/src/runner/runner.ts:300-405`). JSON-schema assertions are shallow (`apifn/collections/src/runner/assertions.ts:98-150`). Reporter callbacks are not consistently isolated, so reporter failure can affect a run. URL logging includes the query string, which can contain credentials (`apifn/core/src/integrations/logfn.ts:67-74`).

**Positive boundary:** script execution disables `require`, `process`, network globals, eval/code generation and enforces a VM timeout (`apifn/collections/src/runner/script-sandbox.ts:112-180`, `apifn/collections/src/runner/script-sandbox.ts:191-252`). Cross-origin redirects strip authorization/cookies and cookie domains are checked (`apifn/collections/src/runner/http-client.ts:102-116`, `apifn/collections/src/runner/http-client.ts:223-233`).

#### APIFN-010 — Medium — React/Svelte Try-It surfaces are incomplete and Svelte has static compile defects

**Evidence: static.** React renders header state without a complete editing path and cannot configure required API-key metadata (`apifn/react/src/TryIt.tsx:115-164`, `apifn/react/src/TryIt.tsx:256-267`). Path values are not encoded and requests lack abort, timeout, and response limits (`apifn/react/src/TryIt.tsx:166-203`). Svelte has the same boundary and hard-codes `X-API-Key` (`apifn/svelte/src/TryIt.svelte:37-70`). `ApiExplorer.svelte` uses `RateLimitInfo` without importing it and selects a `perf` tab excluded from the declared tab type (`apifn/svelte/src/ApiExplorer.svelte:9-17`, `apifn/svelte/src/ApiExplorer.svelte:60`, `apifn/svelte/src/ApiExplorer.svelte:220-232`). Both packages' test scripts report “No tests configured” (`apifn/react/package.json:16-20`, `apifn/svelte/package.json:44-48`).

#### APIFN-011 — Medium — Python SDK is a non-equivalent subset

**Evidence: static.** Collection loading handles one embedded root YAML rather than the specified directory tree (`apifn/python/apifn/collections.py:34-46`). The runner omits scripts, full assertions, retries, parallelism, reporting, and related semantics (`apifn/python/apifn/collections.py:49-134`). Diff covers only endpoints/basic required parameters (`apifn/python/apifn/diff.py:26-82`). Generated OpenAPI includes a nondeterministic timestamp and can expose configuration (`apifn/python/apifn/openapi.py:10-27`). Flask introspection is shallow (`apifn/python/apifn/flask.py:32-73`).

#### APIFN-012 — Medium — Package exports and release metadata are not publish-ready

**Evidence: static.** Core exports `./types` (`apifn/core/package.json:9-19`) but its build only names `src/index.ts` (`apifn/core/tsup.config.ts:3-9`). docsfn has the analogous export/build gap. TypeScript versions are split across 0.0.2–0.0.3 and Python is 0.0.1, far from the specified coordinated 1.0.0. React/Svelte tests are placeholders. Python hard-depends on both FastAPI and Flask while also duplicating them in optional extras (`apifn/python/pyproject.toml:10-21`). The root README is not sufficient release documentation for this multi-package product.

#### APIFN-013 — Medium — Watch/log integration is not robustly wired

**Evidence: static.** Watch response parsing trusts arbitrary JSON and asynchronous middleware/warning paths can expose endpoint URLs (`apifn/core/src/integrations/watchfn.ts:110-170`, `apifn/core/src/integrations/watchfn.ts:204-270`). Static search finds `createCliLogger` only in its definition/tests, not the CLI command path, leaving `LOG-002` unmet. Metrics types are present but the external watchfn contract and deployed behavior are unverified.

#### APIFN-014 — Low — Bundle accounting can hide missing review coverage

**Evidence: directly verified.** `INTENT_AUDIT.md:108-116` reports 103 requirements; the audited `REQUIREMENTS.md` contains 141 unique IDs. Any completion percentage derived from 103 can omit 38 normative obligations.

### Security, validation, and tenant boundaries

- **Blocking:** stored XSS/network exposure in serve; mock network/CORS defaults; missing allocation-boundary limits; auth precedence/error leakage; query-string logging.
- ApiFn is not itself a multi-tenant datastore, but it transports credentials and connects to deployed APIs. Its effective tenant boundary is the collection/environment/token context. That boundary is weakened by auth override ambiguity, environment shape casting, arbitrary URLs, and observable query strings.
- Redaction, redirect credential stripping, cookie-domain checks, sandbox restrictions, and collection write path validation are strong positive invariants. They do not compensate for the exposed serve/mock surfaces.

### Determinism, limits, and errors

- Deterministic sorting exists in generation/diff paths and snippet generation is consistently specified/implemented.
- Most normative caps are checked too late or not at all. In particular, reading a full response before truncation defeats the memory cap.
- Several broad catches transform parse/IO failures into misleading “missing” or placeholder behavior. Production tooling should preserve typed causes, stable exit codes, and safe user-facing diagnostics.

### Compatibility and migrations

- OpenAPI 3.1 output and 3.0 import have useful primitives but not full declared semantics.
- OpenCollection/Bruno compatibility is externally unverified and local write-back is lossy.
- React/Svelte and TypeScript/Python surfaces are not behaviorally equivalent.
- There is no actionable migration/version coordination plan from 0.0.x packages to the specified 1.0 contract.

### Operational, release, and packaging readiness

- No production-safe loopback/host/CORS policy for serve/mock.
- No demonstrated telemetry integration, health behavior, capacity/load envelope, or failure-recovery runbook.
- Workflow placement/package invocation defects block the intended CI gate.
- Export/build mismatches, split versions, placeholder test scripts, and heavy Python dependencies block a trustworthy release.

### Tests and command results

| Check | Result | Evidence class |
|---|---|---|
| Pinned revision | `721eefdd9cd716894e5329123a9e2fb615783611` | Directly verified |
| Working tree before audit artifacts | Clean | Directly verified |
| File/spec/manifest inventories | Completed | Directly verified |
| Requirement-ID parse | 141 unique IDs; bundle claims 103 | Directly verified |
| Existing tests/fixtures | Inventoried; not executed | Static/unverified runtime |
| Build/lint/typecheck/unit/integration/Python/browser | Not run under read-only/no-artifact constraint | Unverified |
| Bruno, registry, CI, authfn/watchfn/secfn/logfn/testfn services | Not exercised | Unverified external |

### Positive invariants

- Collection writer rejects traversal/unsafe output paths.
- HTTP redirects strip sensitive headers cross-origin and cookie domains are validated.
- Script sandbox removes ambient network/process/module capabilities and sets a timeout.
- Core generator/diff and snippet outputs contain deliberate deterministic ordering.
- Redaction utilities and security integration entry points exist.
- Mock request bodies have a 10 MB cap when validation is enabled.
- Package manifests generally declare explicit entry points and licenses, providing a tractable base for release repair.

### External gaps

- Real Bruno/OpenCollection round-trip compatibility.
- Browser rendering, CSP behavior, accessibility, and malicious-spec tests.
- npm/PyPI pack/install/registry integrity and supported Node/Python matrices.
- CI workflow invocation in a consumer repository.
- Live authfn, secfn, logfn, watchfn, and testfn contract compatibility.
- Load, concurrency, timeout, memory, and recovery tests against real endpoints.
- Release signing/provenance, vulnerability scanning, and published migration guidance.

## Recommendations (ranked)

Fix in this order:

1. **Contain exploitable surfaces:** remove `innerHTML`, loopback-bind serve/mock, add explicit host/CORS policy and CSP, redact URLs/upstream errors, and add malicious-input tests.
2. **Enforce limits at allocation boundaries:** streaming body cap, bounded file parsing/depth/routes/items/diffs, integer finite timeouts/concurrency/TTL, AbortSignal propagation, bounded output/history.
3. **Repair contracts:** authfn request/override semantics, JSON Schema draft, OpenAPI collision/dedup/3.0 conversion, OpenCollection schema validation and lossless round trip.
4. **Make the documented product runnable:** complete the explorer/router/proxy surface; export/build docsfn components; fix Svelte type errors and Try-It request controls.
5. **Correct mock and runner semantics:** standards-valid CORS, `$ref`/constraint-aware validation/generation, aborting timeouts, specified retries, reporter isolation, stable typed errors.
6. **Restore distribution integrity:** align package exports/build entries, remove placeholder tests, rationalize Python extras, coordinate versions, and validate packed artifacts in isolated consumers.
7. **Move/fix CI and prove compatibility:** root-level reusable workflow, invoke the correct CLI package/bin, add package/Python/UI matrices, Bruno round trips, and external integration contract tests.
8. **Close parity/documentation gaps:** define intentional TypeScript/Python and React/Svelte differences, add migrations/runbooks, and reconcile the 141-requirement ledger before a release candidate.

Production gate: do not ship a public 1.0 release until APIFN-001 through APIFN-007 are closed, all FAIL requirements are green, the one external interoperability requirement is verified, package artifacts are consumer-tested, and CI exercises the supported matrices.

## Appendix: commands run + environment details

### Environment and commands

- Environment: Darwin arm64; shell `zsh`; detached Git worktree at `721eefdd9cd716894e5329123a9e2fb615783611`; audit launcher Codex Desktop.
- Read-only repository checks: `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git status --porcelain`, and targeted `git ls-tree`/symlink inspection where relevant.
- Inventories/searches: `find apifn ...`, `rg ... apifn`, `wc -l`, `sed`/`nl` for line evidence, and `jq` over package manifests.
- Static requirement accounting: parsed requirement IDs from the bundle and reconciled them against intent/spec/test-vector/phase mappings.
- Intentionally not run: install, build, lint, typecheck, unit/integration/browser/Python tests, package pack/publish, services, or CI.

### Package inventory

| Surface | Published name/version | Readiness note |
|---|---|---|
| Core | `@apifn/core` 0.0.2 | Subpath build/export mismatch; OpenAPI/schema gaps. |
| Collections | `@apifn/collections` 0.0.2 | Shallow validation/lossy round trip. |
| CLI | `@apifn/cli` 0.0.2 | Bin exists; serve and CI path unsafe/broken. |
| Mock | `@apifn/mock` 0.0.2 | Unsafe defaults/incomplete validation. |
| Snippets | `@apifn/snippets` 0.0.3 | Strongest statically complete surface. |
| docsfn | `@apifn/docsfn` 0.0.2 | Required component/runtime surface not exported. |
| React | `@apifn/react` 0.0.2 | Incomplete request controls; placeholder tests. |
| Svelte | `@apifn/svelte` 0.0.2 | Static type/compile defects; placeholder tests. |
| Python | `apifn` 0.0.1 | Subset implementation; dependency packaging issue. |

### Evidence boundaries

- Source locations are relative to the repository and therefore portable.
- Line evidence refers to the pinned commit only.
- “Pass” never implies registry, browser, external-service, or CI proof unless stated.
- Prior ApiFn audit documents and phase completion reports were read only to understand historical claims and were excluded from compliance evidence.

{"id":"2fdca7be-5d24-4ac9-86e9-3107937e1114","title":"ApiFn production-readiness audit — 2026-08-11","content":"# ApiFn production-readiness audit

## Metadata

* Audit date: 2026-08-11
* Auditor: `audit_api_search`
* Model: GPT-5 (Codex)
* Launcher: Codex Desktop
* Repository state: detached `HEAD` at `721eefdd9cd716894e5329123a9e2fb615783611`
* Scope root: `apifn/`
* Method: independent, read-only source and specification review. Existing audit conclusions were not used as compliance evidence.
* Evidence labels:
  * **Directly verified**: observed in the pinned tree or produced by a read-only command in this audit.
  * **Static**: conclusion from source/configuration inspection; the relevant runtime was not executed.
  * **Unverified**: requires a build, package, browser, external service, registry, or CI environment that was not exercised.
* Overall decision: **NO-GO for production**. One critical exploit path and six high-severity correctness, security, interoperability, and release blockers remain.

## Audit scope

This audit covers the complete ApiFn product surface present at the pinned commit:

* TypeScript packages: `apifn/core`, `apifn/collections`, `apifn/cli`, `apifn/mock`, `apifn/snippets`, `apifn/docsfn`, `apifn/react`, and `apifn/svelte`.
* Python distribution: `apifn/python`, including FastAPI and Flask adapters.
* Cross-function integrations: authfn, secfn, logfn, watchfn, testfn, and docsfn integration code owned by ApiFn.
* Public documentation, examples, CI example/workflow, package manifests, exports, build/test scripts, release metadata, fixtures, and tests.
* ApiFn intent plus the complete specification bundle, including all principal documents, 26 phase files, and 26 phase reports. Phase reports and prior audits were treated as historical claims only; implementation was checked independently.

The static inventory contains **251 regular files** under `apifn/` after excluding generated/dependency directories. The largest areas are `.conduct` (62), collections (42), core (36), CLI (32), snippets (20), Python (13), React (13), Svelte (11), docsfn (10), mock (9), examples (1), and the root README (1). Fifty test-related/fixture files and approximately 292 `it`/`test` declarations were found by static search; neither count is a claim that those tests execute or pass.

## Inputs audited (intent + spec bundles)

### Authoritative intent and product documentation

* `apifn/.conduct/intent-v0.md`
* `apifn/README.md`
* Package READMEs, inline API documentation, `apifn/examples/`, and `apifn/examples/ci-cd/github-actions.yml`

### Specification bundle

Bundle: `apifn/.conduct/specs/2026-03-05-new-k4m7x9r2-spec/`

* Principal documents: `INTENT_AUDIT.md`, `SPEC.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `TEST_VECTORS.md`, `PLAN.md`, and `logs.csv`.
* Plans: `phases/PHASE_00.md` through `phases/PHASE_25.md` (26/26 inventoried and inspected).
* Completion claims: `phase-reports/PHASE_00_REPORT.md` through `phase-reports/PHASE_25_REPORT.md` (26/26 inventoried and inspected as non-authoritative history).
* Parsed requirement inventory: **141 unique requirement IDs**. This conflicts with the bundle's statement that there are 103 requirements.

### Runtime, packaging, and verification inputs

* All `src/` trees, adapters/integrations, tests, fixtures, examples, `package.json`, `tsup.config.ts`, TypeScript/Vitest configurations, Python `pyproject.toml`, and workflow YAML under `apifn/`.
* Commands used: pinned-commit/status checks; `find`, `rg`, and `jq` inventories; requirement-ID parsing and manifest/export/script inspection.
* Not run: package installation, build, lint, unit/integration tests, browser tests, Python tests, package packing/publishing, live mock/serve processes, external integrations, or CI. The audit was constrained to read-only work and did not install dependencies or create build/test artifacts.

## High-level findings

| Severity | Count | Headline |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Critical | 1 | `apifn serve` inserts specification-controlled text into `innerHTML`, exposes the service on all interfaces, and enables wildcard CORS. |
| High | 6 | Resource caps are mostly declarative; authfn and OpenAPI contracts diverge; docs generation and mocking are materially incomplete; the documented CI path is not runnable as published. |
| Medium | 6 | Collection fidelity, runner semantics, UI adapters, Python parity, package exports, and observability remain incomplete or unsafe. |
| Low | 1 | Requirement accounting undercounts the normative requirement set by 38 IDs. |

Coverage verdict across the 141 normative IDs: **77 PASS, 48 PARTIAL, 15 FAIL, 1 UNVERIFIED**. A PASS below means the requirement is supported by direct/static source evidence, not that runtime acceptance tests passed.

## Intent Inventory

The bundle identifies 35 intent items. The following inventory preserves the bundle's mapping while recording implementation outcome at the feature level.

| # | Intent | Requirement coverage | Implementation outcome |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Generate OpenAPI 3.1 from HTTP routes | INTRO, OPENAPI | Partial: generation exists; deduplication, collision handling, caps, and full 3.0 conversion do not. |
| 2 | Zod/TypeBox schema validation | SCHEMA | Partial: integrations exist; the declared draft and validation API diverge. |
| 3 | Git-native OpenCollection YAML | COLL | Partial: reader/writer exists, but validation is shallow and fidelity/interoperability is unproven. |
| 4 | Breaking-change detection | DIFF | Partial: deterministic diff exists; caps and several compatibility semantics are incomplete. |
| 5 | Environment sets | ENV | Partial: core resolution exists; ordinary process-environment precedence and caps are incomplete. |
| 6 | React and Svelte API explorer | UI-R, UI-S | Partial: React is usable statically; Svelte has compile/type defects and both lack real tests. |
| 7 | Try-it plus live performance overlay | UI-R/UI-S, WATCH | Partial: UI and watch integration exist but are unsafe/incomplete. |
| 8 | Request history and response diff | UI-R/UI-S | Partial: local components exist; specified persistence/caps and verification are incomplete. |
| 9 | `apifn serve` | CLI, SERVE | Fail: unsafe static HTML shell, no complete explorer/router/proxy behavior. |
| 10 | `apifn test` and collection runner | CLI, RUN, ASSERT | Partial: runner is substantial; cancellation, retries, limits, and reporting isolation diverge. |
| 11 | `apifn diff` | CLI, CI | Partial: command exists; CI/release path is broken. |
| 12 | `apifn export` | CLI | Partial: command exists; normalization/size and interoperability remain incomplete/unverified. |
| 13 | docsfn API reference component | DOCS | Fail: the package does not export/build the required renderer surface. |
| 14 | Embedded docs try-it | DOCS | Fail: no complete embedded runtime integration. |
| 15 | docsfn auto-sidebar | DOCS | Partial: generated pages exist but tag/slug semantics are lossy. |
| 16 | FastAPI/Flask introspection | PY | Partial: adapters exist but are shallow and lack TypeScript parity. |
| 17 | Self-hosted | Architectural | Present, but exposed defaults are unsafe for production. |
| 18 | Git-native collections | COLL | Partial for the same fidelity/interoperability reasons as item 3. |
| 19 | Schema-from-code with no separate YAML | INTRO, OPENAPI | Partial: route introspection exists, but schema semantics are incomplete. |
| 20 | Endpoint performance data | WATCH | Partial: metrics types/integration exist; robust runtime behavior is not established. |
| 21 | Embedded docs site | DOCS | Fail at the required public/package surface. |
| 22 | Breaking-change CI | DIFF, CLI, CI | Fail as a consumable workflow despite working diff primitives. |
| 23 | authfn short-lived test tokens | AUTH | Partial: integration exists but violates the specified request/expiry/override contract. |
| 24 | secfn and logfn integration | SEC, LOG | Partial: redaction exists; CLI logging and URL leakage remain. |
| 25 | p50/p95/p99, error rate, volume via watchfn | WATCH | Partial: types and display paths exist; external contract was not verified. |
| 26 | Postman/Bruno-like API documentation and testing | RUN, ASSERT | Partial: meaningful runner functionality exists, not production parity. |
| 27 | Automatic docs generation | DOCS | Fail at package integration/rendering surface. |
| 28 | Deployed API monitoring via watchfn | WATCH | Partial and externally unverified. |
| 29 | OpenCollection/Bruno interoperability | COLL | Unverified externally; local format handling is only partial. |
| 30 | Comparable core capabilities to Postman/Bruno/Swagger/Scalar | Positioning | Not achieved at production quality. |
| 31 | Mock server | MOCK | Partial: server works statically but validation, generation, CORS, and binding are unsafe. |
| 32 | Code snippets | SNIP | Pass statically across all seven requirements. |
| 33 | GitHub Actions integration | CI | Fail as located/documented. |
| 34 | testfn adapter | TESTFN | Pass statically; live package compatibility remains unverified. |
| 35 | Multi-framework UI | UI-R, UI-S | Partial; Svelte is not release-ready. |

## Intent → Spec coverage matrix

| Intent(s) | SPEC area | Requirement IDs | Bundle test vectors/phases |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1, 19 | Core generation, introspection rules | INTRO-001–005; OPENAPI-001–010 | TV-INTRO/OPENAPI; phases 02, 04 |
| 2 | Schema descriptors and validation | SCHEMA-001–005 | TV-SCHEMA; phase 03 |
| 3, 18, 29 | OpenCollection YAML and Bruno interop | COLL-001–007 | TV-COLL; phases 06–07 |
| 4, 11, 22 | OpenAPI diff, CLI, and CI | DIFF-001–009; CLI-005; CI-001–004 | TV-DIFF/CLI/CI; phases 13–14, 25 |
| 5 | Environment semantics | ENV-001–005 | TV-ENV; phase 08 |
| 6, 35 | React/Svelte explorers | UI-R-001–009; UI-S-001–009 | TV-UI; phases 18–19 |
| 7 | Try-it and performance overlay | UI-R-004/007; UI-S-004/007 | Corresponding TV-UI; phases 18–19, 21 |
| 8 | Request history and response diff | UI-R-005–006; UI-S-005–006 | Corresponding TV-UI; phases 18–19 |
| 9 | Local explorer server | CLI-006; SERVE-001–004 | TV-CLI/SERVE; phase 17 |
| 10, 26 | Collection execution/assertions | CLI-004; RUN-001–011; ASSERT-001–007 | TV-RUN/ASSERT; phases 10–12 |
| 12 | OpenAPI export | CLI-003 | TV-CLI-003; phase 09 |
| 13–15, 21, 27 | docsfn reference, try-it, navigation | DOCS-001–006 | TV-DOCS; phase 20 |
| 16 | Python SDK/adapters | PY-001–005 | TV-PY; phase 24 |
| 17, 30 | Self-hosting and product positioning | Architectural goals/non-goals | Whole plan; no discrete acceptance ID |
| 20, 25, 28 | watchfn integration | WATCH-001–004 | TV-WATCH; phase 21 |
| 23 | authfn token minting | AUTH-001–003 | TV-AUTH; phase 22 |
| 24 | secfn/logfn | SEC-001–002; LOG-001–002 | TV-SEC/LOG; phase 22 |
| 31 | Mock server | MOCK-001–007 | TV-MOCK; phases 16–17 |
| 32 | Snippet generation | SNIP-001–007 | TV-SNIP; phase 15 |
| 33 | GitHub Actions | CI-001–004 | TV-CI; phase 25 |
| 34 | testfn adapter | TESTFN-001–003 | TV-TESTFN; phase 23 |

The matrix has no unmapped intent item. The gap is implementation and verification, not missing spec traceability. The architectural intents (17 and 30) lack independently testable acceptance IDs.

## Requirement coverage summary

| Category | Total | PASS | PARTIAL | FAIL | UNVERIFIED |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| CORE | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| INTRO | 5 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| SCHEMA | 5 | 3 | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| OPENAPI | 13 | 10 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| COLL | 7 | 2 | 3 | 1 | 1 |
| ENV | 5 | 3 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| CLI | 11 | 6 | 4 | 1 | 0 |
| RUN | 11 | 5 | 6 | 0 | 0 |
| ASSERT | 7 | 6 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| DIFF | 9 | 6 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
